- Monthly local-visibility report

Tools & platforms: Google Business Profile, Google Maps, Google Search Console, Bing Places, Justdial, BrightLocal, Google Sheets
Pricing model: One-time setup fee per location, with an optional monthly retainer for posts, reviews, Q&A and reporting; multi-location businesses are scoped by number of profiles.

### FAQ
Q: What is local SEO?
A: Local SEO is the practice of getting a business to appear in Google's map pack, on Google Maps and in "near me" searches for its area, mainly by optimising its Google Business Profile, earning reviews, keeping business details consistent across the web and building location pages. gaa-tha sets this up and runs it monthly for stores, showrooms, clinics, PGs and factories.

Q: How do I get into the top three on Google Maps?
A: Google ranks local results on relevance, distance and prominence. You control relevance (correct categories, complete services, keyword-rich descriptions) and prominence (review count and recency, photos, posts, consistent citations, links from your website). Distance you cannot change, which is why multi-outlet businesses need a profile per location.

Q: Is a Google Business Profile free?
A: Yes. Creating and managing a Google Business Profile is free, and so is appearing on Google Maps. What costs time is doing it properly and keeping it active; that is the part we handle, as a one-time setup or on a monthly retainer.

Q: How do we get more Google reviews?
A: Ask at the right moment, make it effortless and reply to every one. We give your staff a QR code for the counter, WhatsApp follow-up templates for after purchase or delivery and a short script, and we respond to reviews within a day. We never buy or fake reviews; Google removes them and can suspend the profile.

Q: Can you manage several outlets or franchise locations?
A: Yes. We set up one verified profile per location, manage them from a single business group, keep hours, offers and photos consistent, and build a local landing page for each outlet on your website so every profile has a matching page to link to.

Q: How long does local SEO take to work?
A: Profile setup and verification take about two to three weeks. Calls and direction requests usually start rising within the first one to three months as reviews, photos and posts accumulate, and the position holds as long as the profile stays active.

Q: What documents does Google need to verify my business?
A: Verification is usually by video call, postcard or phone, and Google may ask for proof such as a signboard, business registration, utility bill or GST certificate showing the name and address. Requirements change by category, so we check the current method for your business before starting.

Q: My profile has been suspended or has a duplicate — can you fix it?
A: Usually, yes. Suspensions typically come from keyword-stuffed names, mismatched addresses, virtual offices or duplicate listings. We correct the profile to Google's guidelines, gather the evidence and file the reinstatement or merge request, then keep the profile compliant.


## Influencer & UGC Marketing
https://gaa-tha.com/services/influencer-ugc-marketing
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha is an influencer and UGC marketing agency in India that finds and vets creators your audience already trusts — local city influencers, category creators and everyday customers — then briefs them, produces collab reels and UGC videos, secures usage rights so the content can run as ads, and reports on reach, engagement and tracked sales or enquiries.

Best for: D2C beauty and food, FMCG, retail stores, restaurants, real estate and consumer apps
Timeline: Campaigns in 3–6 weeks; always-on programmes run monthly
Engagement model: Campaign fee or monthly retainer, plus creator fees agreed per campaign
Channels/platforms: Instagram, YouTube and YouTube Shorts, Facebook, LinkedIn for B2B

### What it is
Influencer marketing is partnering with creators who already have an audience's trust so they feature a brand in their own content; UGC (user-generated content) marketing is commissioning authentic, creator-made videos and photos for the brand to use in its own ads, pages and listings. The first borrows an audience, the second borrows a voice — and the strongest campaigns use both.

At gaa-tha creator work is planned like media, not like a favour. We shortlist creators by audience fit and real engagement rather than follower count, write briefs and scripts that keep the message on-strategy while leaving room for the creator's style, negotiate usage rights upfront, and track every collaboration with codes and links so the report shows enquiries and sales, not just views.

### What's included
- Creator discovery and vetting — audience location, demographics, engagement quality and past brand work
- Campaign strategy — objective, creator tiers (nano, micro, macro), formats and budget split
- Briefs, scripts and hooks for each creator, with brand do's and don'ts
- Negotiation, contracts and usage-rights agreements for paid and barter collaborations
- Collab reels and Instagram page collaborations so content appears on both profiles
- UGC video production — creator-shot testimonials, unboxings and demos for ads and product pages
- Product seeding, shipping coordination and content approval rounds
- Tracking codes, UTM links and WhatsApp keywords per creator
- ASCI-compliant disclosure guidance for every post
- Performance report on reach, engagement, clicks, codes redeemed and cost per result

### How we work
1. Objective and creator map — We agree what the campaign must do — awareness in a city, launches, sales — and build a shortlist of creators whose audience actually matches yours.
2. Vetting and outreach — Shortlisted creators are checked for real engagement and audience location, then contacted with a clear offer, timeline and usage terms.
3. Briefs and production — Each creator receives a brief, hooks and a script outline; UGC creators shoot to a shot list and we edit where the content will run as ads.
4. Publish and amplify — Content goes live on schedule as collab posts, and the best-performing pieces are boosted or run as Meta ads with the rights already secured.
5. Track and report — Codes, links and platform insights are collected into one report on reach, engagement and tracked enquiries or sales, with recommendations for the next round.

### Deliverables
- Vetted creator shortlist with audience data and rates
- Campaign brief, scripts and content calendar
- Signed usage-rights agreements per creator
- Published collab reels and posts, plus edited UGC videos for ads
- Tracking sheet with codes, links and per-creator results
- Post-campaign performance report

Tools & platforms: Instagram Collabs, Meta Business Suite, YouTube Studio, Google Sheets, Bitly, CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro
Pricing model: Campaign fee or monthly retainer for strategy, management, production and reporting; creator fees are agreed per campaign and shown transparently in the plan.

### FAQ
Q: What is the difference between influencer marketing and UGC?
A: Influencer marketing pays a creator to feature your brand on their own profile, so you reach their audience. UGC (user-generated content) pays a creator or customer to make authentic-looking video or photos that you publish on your own channels, ads and product pages. gaa-tha runs both, often in the same campaign, with usage rights sorted upfront.

Q: How much do influencers charge in India?
A: It ranges from product-only barter for nano creators to significant fees for macro creators and celebrities, and it changes with platform, format, exclusivity and usage rights. We share a rate card for your shortlist before anything is committed and plan the creator mix to your budget rather than the other way round.

Q: How do you choose creators and avoid fake followers?
A: By audience fit first — where their followers live, their age and interests — and then by engagement quality: comments that read like real people, view-to-follower ratios and consistency across recent posts. We check past brand collaborations and audience location data before proposing anyone.

Q: Who owns the content and can we use it in ads?
A: Only if the agreement says so, which is why usage rights are negotiated before the shoot. We specify where the content can be used (ads, website, marketplace listings, in-store screens), for how long, and whether the creator's face and name can appear in paid media.

Q: How do you measure influencer marketing ROI?
A: Each creator gets a unique code, link or WhatsApp keyword, and we combine that with platform insights to report reach, engagement, profile visits, clicks, codes redeemed and cost per result. For awareness campaigns we also track branded search and follower growth during the campaign window.

Q: Can we do barter collaborations instead of paid ones?
A: Yes, particularly with nano and micro creators and local city influencers, where product, meals or experiences are a fair exchange. Barter works best for seeding and reviews; for guaranteed deliverables, timelines and usage rights, a paid agreement is more reliable.

Q: Do influencer posts need to be marked as ads?
A: Yes. ASCI guidelines in India require clear disclosure such as #ad or #collab on paid or barter collaborations. We include the disclosure in every brief and check it before posts go live.

Q: How many creators does a campaign need?
A: It depends on the objective. A city launch might use ten to twenty nano and micro creators for saturation; a product launch might pair a few category creators with a batch of UGC videos for ads. We size the mix to budget and reach goals in the plan, not to a fixed package.


## B2B & Export Lead Generation
https://gaa-tha.com/services/b2b-lead-generation
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha runs B2B and export lead generation for Indian manufacturers, packaging, machinery and bulk food suppliers: ideal-buyer and country targeting, LinkedIn decision-maker lists and outreach sequences, Meta and LinkedIn lead ads, IndiaMART and TradeIndia listing optimisation, WhatsApp first-reply templates and a lead-qualification SOP with a CRM or Excel tracker, so enquiries turn into quotes and orders.

Best for: Manufacturers, exporters, packaging, machinery, industrial coatings and bulk food suppliers
Timeline: Setup in 2–3 weeks; first outreach cycles in month one; then monthly
Engagement model: Monthly retainer; ad spend and platform subscriptions paid directly by you
Channels/platforms: LinkedIn, Meta lead ads, Google Search, IndiaMART, TradeIndia, WhatsApp, email

### What it is
B2B lead generation is the systematic work of finding the companies that should be buying from you, reaching the right person inside them and turning the first reply into a qualified enquiry — through LinkedIn outreach, targeted ads, B2B marketplaces such as IndiaMART and TradeIndia, search and email. Export lead generation applies the same system to buyers in specific countries.

At gaa-tha the lead system is built before the outreach starts: who the ideal buyer is, which countries and categories, what the first message says, who replies on WhatsApp and within how long, and how every lead is tagged so the monthly report shows quotes and orders rather than a count of messages sent. The channels are then run together, with the tracker as the single source of truth.

### What's included
- Ideal-buyer profile and country or region targeting by product, capacity and margin
- LinkedIn company and decision-maker lists built for each target segment
- LinkedIn profile and company-page optimisation for the founder and sales team
- Outreach sequences — connection notes, follow-ups and email — written to earn a reply, not to spam
- Meta and LinkedIn lead-generation ads with instant forms and WhatsApp click-to-chat
- Google Search campaigns for product and export-intent keywords
- IndiaMART and TradeIndia listing optimisation — catalogue, titles, images, specifications and pricing
- WhatsApp first-reply templates and a response-time SOP for your sales team
- Lead-qualification SOP — questions, scoring and hand-off rules
- CRM or Excel tracker with a dashboard, and a monthly report on leads, qualified leads, quotes and orders

### How we work
1. Buyer profile and targets — We define the ideal buyer with your sales team — industry, size, country, order value — and agree what a qualified lead means and how many quotes a month is the goal.
2. Assets and lists — LinkedIn profiles, company page, product one-pagers and marketplace listings are brought up to standard, and decision-maker lists are built per segment.
3. Outreach and ads — Sequences go live on LinkedIn and email, lead ads run on Meta and LinkedIn, and search campaigns catch buyers already looking — all pointing to one WhatsApp or form.
4. Qualify and hand off — Every reply is answered with the first-reply template, scored against the SOP and handed to sales with context in the tracker.
5. Review and refine — A monthly review with the sales team on lead quality, quote conversion and which channel or segment produced the best buyers, then the lists and messages are adjusted.

### Deliverables
- Ideal-buyer profile and country or segment targeting document
- Optimised LinkedIn profiles, company page and marketplace listings
- Outreach sequences and lead-ad campaigns live
- WhatsApp first-reply templates and lead-qualification SOP
- CRM or Excel lead tracker with dashboard
- Monthly report on leads, qualified leads, quotes and orders by channel

Tools & platforms: LinkedIn Sales Navigator, LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, IndiaMART Seller, TradeIndia, WhatsApp Business, Google Sheets
Pricing model: Monthly retainer scoped to channels, countries and outreach volume; ad spend and tools such as LinkedIn Sales Navigator or marketplace subscriptions are paid directly by you.

### FAQ
Q: What is B2B lead generation?
A: B2B lead generation is the process of identifying the companies that should buy from you, reaching the decision-maker and converting the first conversation into a qualified enquiry — using LinkedIn outreach, targeted ads, B2B marketplaces, search and email. gaa-tha runs it as one system with a tracker, so your sales team sees qualified leads, not raw messages.

Q: Do you generate B2B and export leads for manufacturers?
A: Yes. Manufacturers, exporters, packaging, machinery, industrial coatings and bulk food suppliers are the businesses we do this for most. We combine LinkedIn outreach to buyers in target countries, lead ads, IndiaMART and TradeIndia optimisation and search campaigns with a WhatsApp reply SOP so enquiries turn into quotes.

Q: Which countries can you target for export leads?
A: Any country where LinkedIn, Google and email reach buyers — typically the Middle East, Africa, Europe, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia and South-East Asia for Indian exporters. We prioritise by your product's demand, import regulations, freight economics and where you already have references.

Q: Does LinkedIn outreach actually work, or is it spam?
A: It works when the list is precise and the message is about the buyer's problem, not your company profile. We keep volumes modest, personalise by segment, follow up politely a limited number of times and stop when there is no interest, which is what keeps reply rates healthy and accounts safe.

Q: IndiaMART or our own website — which is better for leads?
A: Both, for different buyers. IndiaMART and TradeIndia bring high-volume domestic enquiries that need fast qualification; your own website with Google Search and LinkedIn brings fewer but more serious buyers, especially for export. We optimise the marketplace listings and run the website channels together, then compare quote conversion by source.

Q: How many leads will we get a month?
A: It depends on your category, order value, countries and budget, so we do not promise a number before the first month of data. What we agree upfront is the definition of a qualified lead and the monthly quote target, then report against that by channel and adjust the mix to whatever produces buyers who actually order.

Q: How do you qualify leads before they reach our sales team?
A: With a short SOP: a WhatsApp or email first reply within agreed hours, three to five qualifying questions (quantity, application, location, timeline, budget or target price), a score, and a hand-off rule. Junk and price-shoppers are tagged by source so we can cut the channels producing them.

Q: Do we need a website before starting lead generation?
A: A basic, credible one, yes — buyers check it before replying. A single well-built page with products, capacity, certifications, references and a WhatsApp button is enough to start; a full corporate site can follow. We build both under Website Design & Development.


## Campaign Planning (Festive & Launch)
https://gaa-tha.com/services/campaign-planning
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha plans and runs 360° campaigns for Diwali, Navratri, launches and seasonal sales: one campaign idea and key visual, a media plan and budget split across outdoor (store-fronts, auto-rickshaws, buses), Meta ads, influencer collabs, cinema and in-store video and on-ground activation, delivered by one in-house team and closed with a post-campaign report.

Best for: Retail chains, sweets and FMCG brands, real-estate launches, D2C brands and franchise businesses
Timeline: Planning 3–4 weeks before launch; campaigns run 2–8 weeks
Engagement model: Project fee per campaign; media, print and creator budgets agreed upfront
Channels/platforms: Outdoor, Meta ads, Instagram, influencers, cinema, in-store screens, WhatsApp, print

### What it is
Campaign planning is the work of taking one message to market across every channel at once — outdoor, digital ads, social content, influencers, cinema, in-store and on-ground — for a fixed period such as Diwali, a product launch or a season, with one budget, one key visual and one measure of success. A 360° campaign is the opposite of posting a festive creative and hoping.

At gaa-tha a campaign starts with the idea and the number it must move — footfall, launch bookings, orders — and then works backwards to the media plan. Because reels, AI ads, design, Meta ads, influencer management and cinema films are all in-house, the same key visual can become a store-front hoarding, an auto-rickshaw wrap, a reel, a WhatsApp broadcast and a cinema ad without three agencies in the loop.

### What's included
- Campaign idea, message and key visual, adapted to every format and size
- Media plan and budget split across outdoor, digital, influencers, cinema and in-store
- Outdoor — store-front branding, hoardings, auto-rickshaw and bus panels, with vendor coordination
- Meta ads and Instagram content for the campaign window, including reels and AI ad shoots
- Influencer collaborations with local city creators and category creators
- Cinema and in-store video — script, production and placement
- WhatsApp broadcasts, offers and landing page or store-locator setup
- On-ground activation support — launch events, sampling, in-store displays and staff briefing
- Campaign calendar with production deadlines, approvals and go-live dates
- Post-campaign report on reach, engagement, enquiries, footfall or orders against the plan

### How we work
1. Objective and budget — We agree what the campaign must move — footfall, bookings, orders — the dates, the cities and the total budget, then set the one number it will be judged on.
2. Idea and key visual — One campaign idea, headline and key visual are developed and approved, with adaptations planned for every size from a reel to a hoarding.
3. Media plan — Budget is split across outdoor, Meta ads, influencers, cinema and in-store based on where your buyers are during the campaign window, with vendor quotes shown transparently.
4. Produce and launch — Creative is produced in batches, outdoor is printed and installed, creators are briefed, ads and cinema slots go live to the calendar, and store staff are briefed.
5. Monitor and report — Ads and content are optimised daily during the window, and a post-campaign report compares reach, enquiries, footfall or orders with the plan and records what to repeat.

### Deliverables
- Campaign concept, headline and key visual with format adaptations
- Media plan with budget split and vendor quotes
- Print-ready outdoor artwork and installed placements
- Reels, ads, influencer content and cinema or in-store video
- Campaign calendar and on-ground activation plan
- Post-campaign performance report

Tools & platforms: Meta Ads Manager, Instagram, WhatsApp Business, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Premiere Pro, Google Sheets, Canva
Pricing model: Project fee per campaign scoped to channels and production volume; outdoor printing, media, cinema slots and creator fees are quoted upfront and paid at the agreed amounts, with no hidden markup.

### FAQ
Q: What is a 360° marketing campaign?
A: A 360° campaign runs one message across every channel a buyer meets during a fixed window — outdoor, digital ads, social, influencers, cinema, in-store and on-ground — with one budget, one key visual and one measure of success. gaa-tha plans and produces the whole thing with one in-house team so nothing gets lost between vendors.

Q: When should we start planning a Diwali campaign?
A: At least six to eight weeks before the festive window opens, and earlier if outdoor placements or cinema slots are involved because good positions book out. Planning and creative take three to four weeks; production, printing and installation need the rest. The same applies to Navratri, Rakhi and wedding-season campaigns.

Q: How much budget does a festive campaign need?
A: It depends on the cities, the channels and how much production is new, so we plan to the budget you have rather than a minimum. A campaign in one city can be built around store-front branding, a few auto-rickshaws, reels, local creators and Meta ads; a multi-city launch adds hoardings, cinema and more creators. The media plan shows every line before you commit.

Q: Do you handle outdoor printing, permissions and installation?
A: Yes. We design the artwork, get quotes from printing and outdoor vendors, coordinate municipal permissions where required, schedule installation and check the placements are up, and the vendor costs are shown transparently in the media plan.

Q: Do cinema ads work for local brands?
A: For retail, sweets, real estate and local services, yes — a cinema screen in the right multiplex or single-screen puts a large, undistracted local audience in front of a 20–30 second film with no skip button. We produce the film and book the screens by locality so the spend follows your catchment.

Q: How do you measure a campaign that runs outdoor and digital together?
A: By one primary number agreed upfront — footfall, bookings, orders or enquiries — plus channel diagnostics: reach and cost per result for ads, creator reach and codes, WhatsApp keyword responses, store-level sales during the window and branded search volume. The post-campaign report compares all of it with the plan.

Q: Can you plan a launch campaign for a real-estate project or a new store?
A: Yes. Launch campaigns follow the same method: a launch idea and key visual, teaser and launch phases, site or store branding, Meta lead ads or footfall ads, local creators, WhatsApp follow-up and an opening-day activation, reported on site visits, bookings or first-week sales.

Q: What if we only want the digital part of a campaign?
A: That is fine. Many campaigns are digital-only — reels, Meta ads, creators and WhatsApp — and we scope them the same way, with one idea, one calendar and one report. Outdoor, cinema and on-ground can be added later when the budget or the occasion calls for it.


# D2C Ecommerce
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ecommerce

Your own store, built to sell — not just to look good.

D2C Ecommerce is the gaa-tha practice for brands selling from their own website: Shopify stores designed for conversion, multi-outlet builds that route orders to the right store, ongoing store management, conversion-rate optimisation, shopping ads, ecommerce SEO and end-to-end brand launches.

## FAQ
Q: Do you build and manage Shopify stores?
A: Yes. We design and develop Shopify stores (custom themes, custom sections, checkout and payment integrations, tracking) and run monthly store management for product uploads, price changes, banners, apps and fixes.

Q: Shopify or WooCommerce — which should I choose in India?
A: Shopify for most D2C brands: faster to launch, easier to maintain, and the Indian checkout, COD and shipping apps are mature. WooCommerce or a custom build makes sense when you need deep customisation, an existing WordPress site, or very specific B2B pricing logic.

Q: Can one website serve multiple store locations or franchises?
A: Yes. We build multi-location Shopify stores where the customer enters a pincode or picks an outlet, and the order is routed to that outlet with WhatsApp notifications and outlet-level availability and pricing rules.

Q: How long does a Shopify store take?
A: Two to six weeks depending on catalogue size, custom sections and integrations. Migrations from Amazon or another platform add time for product data cleanup.

Q: What does D2C performance marketing include?
A: Meta and Google shopping and catalogue ads, creative testing, ROAS and MER targets, attribution fixes (Conversions API, checkout tracking) and retention flows on email and WhatsApp — all reported against contribution margin, not just ad-platform ROAS.


## Shopify Store Design & Development
https://gaa-tha.com/services/shopify-development
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha designs and develops Shopify stores for Indian D2C brands that are built to convert, not just to look good — custom themes and Liquid sections, GoKwik or Shopflo checkout and Razorpay payments, COD and pincode rules, Meta Pixel, Conversions API and GA4 tracking, and product migration from Amazon or your old platform, delivered in two to six weeks.

Best for: D2C brands in beauty, food, fashion, home and wellness selling from their own site
Timeline: 2–6 weeks depending on catalogue size and integrations
Engagement model: Fixed-scope project; optional monthly maintenance retainer
Channels/platforms: Shopify, Razorpay, GoKwik, Shopflo, Shiprocket, Meta, Google

### What it is
Shopify store design and development is the work of planning, designing and coding an online store on Shopify: the theme and page layouts, custom sections such as kit builders and pincode checkers, checkout and payment integrations, shipping and cash-on-delivery rules, analytics tracking and the product catalogue itself. A good build is judged by how easily a visitor finds, trusts and buys a product on a phone, not by how the homepage looks on a designer's monitor.

At gaa-tha every store starts with a UX audit of what Indian shoppers actually do — browse on mobile, compare on WhatsApp, prefer COD until they trust you — and the theme is built around those habits. The same team handles product photography, copy and the Meta and Google tracking, so the store is ready to run ads on the day it goes live.

### What's included
- UX audit and conversion-first wireframes for home, collection, product, cart and checkout
- Custom Shopify theme, or Liquid customisation of a premium theme
- Custom sections: combo and kit builders, concern-based filters, pincode checkers, product carousels, cart drawers with coupons
- Checkout integrations such as GoKwik, Shopflo and Razorpay with UPI, cards, wallets and EMI
- COD and prepaid rules, partial-payment and COD-verification setup
- Shipping zones, rate rules and pincode serviceability logic
- Meta Pixel and Conversions API, GA4 and Google Tag Manager with verified purchase events
- Product migration from Amazon, Flipkart, WooCommerce or spreadsheets with cleaned titles, variants and images
- Speed optimisation: image compression, app cleanup, script deferral and Core Web Vitals checks
- Launch checklist: domain, SSL, policies, legal pages, abandoned-cart and order notifications

### How we work
1. Audit and scope — We review your catalogue, current site or marketplace listings, margins and customer questions, then agree the page list, integrations and timeline.
2. Wireframes and design — Mobile-first wireframes for the key templates, then a visual design that carries your brand identity into product, collection and cart pages.
3. Build and integrate — Theme development in Liquid, custom sections, checkout, payments, shipping and COD rules, and the Pixel, CAPI and GA4 events.
4. Catalogue and content — Products, variants, collections, images and copy are loaded and checked; migrations are cleaned before import so nothing breaks at launch.
5. Test, launch and hand over — Test orders on every payment method and device, a go-live checklist, and a walkthrough so your team can manage the store day to day.

### Deliverables
- Live Shopify store on your domain with a custom or customised theme
- Configured checkout, payments, shipping and COD rules
- Verified Meta Pixel, Conversions API and GA4 tracking with a purchase-event test log
- Imported, cleaned product catalogue with collections and navigation
- Store admin guide and a recorded walkthrough for your team
- Speed and launch checklist report

Tools & platforms: Shopify, Shopify Liquid, Razorpay, GoKwik, Shopflo, Shiprocket, Meta Conversions API, Google Analytics 4
Pricing model: Fixed-scope project fee based on templates, custom sections and integrations; an optional monthly maintenance retainer covers updates and fixes after launch. Shopify subscription and app charges are paid by you to the platforms.

### FAQ
Q: How long does a Shopify store take to build?
A: Two to six weeks. A store on a customised premium theme with a small catalogue is at the faster end; custom themes, kit builders, pincode logic and migrations from Amazon or another platform add time for design and data cleanup. Content and approvals arriving on time is the biggest factor. gaa-tha shares a week-by-week plan before starting.

Q: Shopify or WooCommerce — which is better for a D2C brand in India?
A: Shopify for most D2C brands: it is faster to launch, easier for your team to maintain, and the Indian checkout, COD, shipping and WhatsApp apps are mature. WooCommerce or a custom build makes sense when you already run WordPress, need deep customisation or have specific B2B pricing logic. We build both and recommend based on your catalogue and team.

Q: Can you move my products from Amazon or Flipkart to Shopify?
A: Yes. We export your listings, clean titles, descriptions, variants, images and pricing, map them to Shopify's product structure and import with collections and tags in place. Marketplace listings are written for marketplace search, so we usually rewrite the key product pages for your own store's buyers.

Q: Which payment and checkout options do you set up?
A: Razorpay, Shopify Payments, PayU or Cashfree for UPI, cards, net banking, wallets and EMI, and one-page checkouts such as GoKwik or Shopflo where they suit your volume. COD is set up with rules — pincode limits, order-value caps and OTP or WhatsApp verification — to reduce returns to origin. Gateway fees are set by the providers and vary; we share the current structure before you choose.

Q: Do you handle the Meta Pixel, Conversions API and GA4 setup?
A: Yes, on every build. Pixel and CAPI are configured for view, add-to-cart, checkout and purchase events, GA4 is connected through Google Tag Manager, and every event is verified with test orders before launch so your ads report real purchases.

Q: Will the store be fast on mobile?
A: It is built to be. Most Indian D2C traffic is on mid-range Android phones over mobile data, so we compress images, limit apps, defer scripts and check Core Web Vitals before go-live. Speed checks continue under a maintenance retainer, because apps added later are the usual cause of slowdowns.

Q: What do I need to give you before the build starts?
A: Your brand identity files, product data (names, descriptions, variants, MRP, images), policies for shipping, returns and privacy, domain access, and your GST and bank details for the payment gateway. If any of these are missing we can produce them — photography, copy and branding are in-house.


## Multi-location Shopify & Local Delivery
https://gaa-tha.com/services/multi-location-shopify-local-delivery
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha builds multi-location Shopify stores for retail chains, franchises and local-delivery brands in India: one website where the customer enters a pincode or picks an outlet, and the order is routed to that store with a WhatsApp notification, outlet-level availability toggles, unified pricing and prepaid or COD rules set per location.

Best for: Retail chains, franchises, sweet and snack shops, bakeries, pharmacies and local-delivery brands
Timeline: 3–6 weeks for the first set of outlets
Engagement model: Project build; optional retainer to add outlets and maintain
Channels/platforms: Shopify, Shopify Locations, WhatsApp Business, pincode and local-delivery apps

### What it is
A multi-location Shopify store is a single ecommerce website that serves several physical outlets: the customer enters a pincode or chooses a store, the site shows what that outlet has in stock and can deliver, and the order is sent to that outlet to fulfil. It replaces the alternatives of one website per branch, or one central warehouse shipping everything by courier, for businesses whose products are made or held locally.

gaa-tha builds these for chains that sell fresh or heavy goods — sweets, snacks, bakery, dairy, pharmacy, groceries — and for franchise networks that want one brand storefront with outlet-level control. Each outlet gets its own WhatsApp order alerts, its own availability switches and its own delivery rules, while the brand keeps one catalogue, one price list and one set of reports.

### What's included
- Location or pincode-based store assignment with a serviceability check before checkout
- Order routing logic to the assigned outlet using Shopify Locations and fulfilment rules
- WhatsApp order notifications to each outlet, with order details and a confirmation step
- Outlet-level availability toggles so a store can switch products off when they run out
- Prepaid-only or COD rules per outlet, per pincode or per order value
- Unified pricing and promotions across outlets, with optional outlet-specific offers
- Local delivery, pick-up and slot options with delivery charges by distance or zone
- Outlet dashboard and staff roles so each store sees only its own orders
- Reporting by outlet: orders, revenue, cancellations and delivery times

### How we work
1. Map the network — We list every outlet, its pincodes or delivery radius, opening hours, product range and who takes the order, then define the routing rules.
2. Design the location flow — The pincode or store-picker experience is designed so a customer knows within seconds which outlet will serve them and what it can deliver.
3. Build routing and notifications — Shopify Locations, fulfilment rules, WhatsApp alerts, availability toggles and prepaid or COD rules are built and tested outlet by outlet.
4. Train the outlets — Store staff get a short guide and a walkthrough for confirming, packing and closing orders, plus a rule for what to do when a product runs out.
5. Launch and expand — The site goes live with a pilot set of outlets, edge cases are fixed in the first two weeks, and new outlets are added from a template.

### Deliverables
- Live Shopify store with pincode or outlet selection and routing rules
- Outlet-wise WhatsApp notification setup and confirmation flow
- Availability, pricing and payment rules configured per outlet
- Outlet onboarding template for adding new stores or franchisees
- Staff guide and recorded walkthrough for outlet teams
- Outlet-level reporting view

Tools & platforms: Shopify, Shopify Locations, Shopify Flow, WhatsApp Business API, Razorpay, Google Maps Platform, Google Sheets
Pricing model: Project fee scoped to the number of outlets, routing complexity and integrations, with an optional monthly retainer to add outlets, tune rules and maintain the store. Shopify, WhatsApp API and app charges are paid by you to the providers.

### FAQ
Q: Can one website serve multiple store locations or franchises?
A: Yes. A multi-location Shopify build lets a customer enter a pincode or pick an outlet, and routes the order to that store with its own notification, stock availability and payment rules. The brand keeps one domain, one catalogue and one set of reports. gaa-tha builds and maintains these for chains and franchise networks across India.

Q: How does the order reach the right outlet?
A: The customer's pincode or chosen store is matched to an outlet during checkout, the order is assigned to that Shopify location, and a WhatsApp message with the order details goes to the outlet's number. Staff confirm from their phone or the outlet dashboard, and the customer receives the usual order and dispatch updates.

Q: What happens if an outlet runs out of a product?
A: Outlet staff switch the product off for their location from a simple toggle, and it stops showing as available to customers in that outlet's pincodes while staying live elsewhere. Rules can also fall back to a nearby outlet or to central dispatch if you prefer.

Q: Can each outlet have its own prices and offers?
A: The default is unified pricing across the brand, which most chains want for trust and simplicity. Outlet-specific offers, delivery charges and minimum order values can be added where a franchise agreement or local competition needs them.

Q: Can we restrict COD to certain locations?
A: Yes. Prepaid-only or COD rules can be set per outlet, per pincode or per order value, which is useful for new outlets, far-away pincodes and high-value orders where returns to origin hurt.

Q: How long does a multi-location store take to build?
A: Three to six weeks for the first set of outlets, depending on how many locations there are, whether the catalogue differs by outlet and which delivery and payment rules you need. Once the template exists, adding a new outlet usually takes days rather than weeks.

Q: Does this work for franchises where each outlet is a separate business?
A: Yes. Each franchisee can receive and fulfil only their own orders, see only their own reports and settle with the brand on whatever terms you agree, while the customer sees one brand and one checkout. We document the roles and the settlement view before building.


## Ecommerce Website Development
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ecommerce-website-development
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha develops ecommerce websites on WordPress and WooCommerce, headless frameworks and custom stacks for Indian brands that need something Shopify does not offer — B2B price lists and quote flows, multi-currency export catalogues, deep ERP integrations or an existing WordPress site — with Razorpay or PayU payments, shipping integrations and full tracking built in.

Best for: B2B sellers, manufacturers and exporters, brands already on WordPress, and stores with custom pricing or catalogue logic
Timeline: 4–10 weeks depending on platform and integrations
Engagement model: Fixed-scope project; optional maintenance and hosting retainer
Channels/platforms: WordPress, WooCommerce, headless (Next.js), custom builds, Razorpay, PayU

### What it is
Ecommerce website development is the design and coding of an online store on a platform other than a hosted builder: WordPress with WooCommerce, a headless front end connected to a commerce back end, or a fully custom application. It suits businesses whose catalogue, pricing or integrations do not fit a standard template — tiered B2B pricing, request-a-quote flows, dealer logins, configurable products or a connection to an existing ERP.

gaa-tha recommends Shopify for most D2C brands and builds elsewhere when there is a clear reason. WooCommerce is the common choice for brands already on WordPress or needing plugin-level control; headless builds are for brands where speed and a custom front end matter; custom applications are for genuinely unusual commerce logic. Whatever the stack, the store ships with Indian payment gateways, shipping integrations, structured data and verified tracking.

### What's included
- Platform recommendation — Shopify, WooCommerce, headless or custom — with reasons
- UX and information architecture for catalogue, product, cart, checkout and account pages
- WooCommerce theme and plugin development, or a headless front end on a commerce API
- B2B features: tiered pricing, dealer or distributor logins, minimum order quantities, request-a-quote
- Payment integration with Razorpay, PayU or Cashfree, plus Stripe or PayPal for international buyers
- Shipping integrations such as Shiprocket and Delhivery, pincode checks and COD rules
- ERP, inventory, CRM or accounting integrations via API or scheduled sync
- Product, Review and Breadcrumb schema, sitemap and technical SEO from day one

### FAQ
Q: When should I choose WooCommerce or a custom build over Shopify?
A: When you already run a WordPress site with content and rankings, need plugin-level control, have B2B pricing or quote logic, sell configurable or made-to-order products, or must integrate tightly with an ERP. For a standard D2C catalogue Shopify is usually faster and cheaper to run. gaa-tha tells you honestly which fits before quoting.

Q: How long does an ecommerce website take to build?
A: Four to ten weeks. A WooCommerce store on a customised theme with a straightforward catalogue sits at the faster end; headless builds, B2B account systems and ERP integrations take longer because of data mapping and testing. Content and product data readiness is the biggest variable.

Q: Can you build a B2B ecommerce site with dealer pricing?
A: Yes. Dealer and distributor logins, tiered or customer-group pricing, minimum order quantities, credit-terms checkout and request-a-quote flows are common in our manufacturer and exporter builds. Prices can be hidden from the public and shown only after approval.

Q: Which payment gateways work for Indian and international buyers?
A: Razorpay, PayU and Cashfree cover UPI, cards, net banking, wallets and EMI for Indian buyers; Stripe or PayPal are added for export customers paying in other currencies. Gateway fees vary by provider and payment method, and we share the current structures before you choose.

Q: Can you connect the store to my ERP or inventory system?
A: Yes, where the system has an API or an export we can schedule. Typical connections sync stock, prices and orders between the store and Tally, Zoho, Busy, SAP Business One or a custom system, so your team is not keying orders twice.

Q: Who hosts and maintains the site after launch?
A: Hosting is in your name on a provider we recommend for your traffic, and you own every login. Maintenance — updates, security patches, backups, speed checks and fixes — is available as a monthly retainer, or your team can take over with our documentation.

Q: Will the site be found on Google and by AI assistants?
A: It is built to be: clean semantic HTML, Product, Review and Breadcrumb schema, fast Core Web Vitals, an XML sitemap, an llms.txt file and answer-first category copy. Ongoing ecommerce SEO is a separate service if you want rankings actively grown.

It is the difference between a store that was launched once and a store that is looked after.

### FAQ
Q: What does Shopify store management include?

## Conversion Rate Optimisation (CRO)
https://gaa-tha.com/services/conversion-rate-optimisation
Last updated: 2026-09-25

Conversion rate optimisation (CRO) at gaa-tha turns more of your existing store visitors into buyers: a funnel and analytics audit, heatmaps and session recordings, fixes to product pages, cart and checkout, trust elements, offer and bundle design, and A/B tests that prove what moved the number before you spend more on ads.

Best for: Shopify and WooCommerce stores with steady traffic and a conversion rate that has plateaued
Timeline: Audit in 2 weeks, then a 3-month test cycle
Engagement model: Fixed-fee audit, then a monthly optimisation retainer
Channels/platforms: Shopify, WooCommerce, Google Analytics 4, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar

### What it is
Conversion rate optimisation (CRO) is the practice of increasing the share of website visitors who complete a purchase, by finding where they hesitate or leave and fixing it with evidence. It uses analytics, heatmaps, session recordings and customer feedback to diagnose problems, then tests changes to product pages, cart, checkout, offers and trust signals to see which actually lift orders.

For Indian D2C stores the usual leaks are predictable: slow mobile pages, product pages that answer none of the buyer's questions, no clarity on size or ingredients, missing COD and delivery information, a cart with no reason to add more and a checkout with too many steps. gaa-tha fixes the obvious problems first, then runs A/B tests on the changes that carry risk, so every improvement is measured rather than assumed.

### What's included
- Funnel and analytics audit: GA4 events, drop-off by step, device and traffic source
- Heatmaps, scroll maps and session recordings on product, cart and checkout pages
- Product page fixes: above-the-fold clarity, image order, variant selectors, FAQs, delivery and COD information
- Cart and checkout fixes: drawer cart, free-shipping progress bar, coupon logic, guest checkout, fewer fields
- Trust elements: reviews, badges, return policy, WhatsApp support and founder story where it helps
- Offer and bundle design: combos, kits, subscriptions and first-order incentives
- A/B and split tests with a hypothesis, sample size and decision rule for each
- Site speed and mobile usability fixes that affect conversion
- Monthly CRO report: conversion rate by device and source, test results and next hypotheses

### How we work
1. Measure — We verify tracking, map the funnel from landing to purchase and find the steps and devices where visitors leave.
2. Diagnose — Heatmaps, recordings, customer-support chats and reviews explain why people leave at those steps.
3. Fix the obvious — Broken, slow or confusing elements are fixed straight away without a test, because the evidence is already clear.
4. Test the rest — Riskier changes — offers, layouts, pricing presentation — run as A/B tests with a hypothesis and a decision rule.
5. Report and repeat — Monthly results by device and source, winning changes made permanent, and the next set of hypotheses agreed.

### Deliverables
- CRO audit report with prioritised fixes and expected impact
- Implemented product, cart and checkout improvements
- Test plan with hypotheses, results and decisions
- Offer and bundle structure for the store
- Monthly conversion report by device and traffic source

Tools & platforms: Google Analytics 4, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar, Shopify, Google Tag Manager, PageSpeed Insights, Judge.me
Pricing model: A fixed-fee audit to start, then a monthly optimisation retainer scoped to the number of tests and the design and development time each month; tool subscriptions are paid by you to the providers.

### FAQ
Q: What is a good ecommerce conversion rate in India?
A: It depends on category, price point and traffic source, so any single benchmark is misleading; stores selling low-ticket consumables convert far better than furniture or jewellery, and returning visitors convert several times better than cold ad traffic. The useful comparison is your own rate by device and source, month on month. gaa-tha sets a baseline in the audit and reports against it.

Q: How long before CRO shows results?
A: The audit takes about two weeks and the first fixes usually go live in the same month. Tests need enough orders to reach a decision, which for most Indian D2C stores means two to six weeks per test, so a meaningful programme runs for at least three months.

Q: Do I need a lot of traffic for A/B testing?
A: For tests, yes — a few hundred orders a month is a practical minimum to reach decisions in reasonable time. Below that, we rely on analytics, recordings and best-practice fixes rather than split tests, and measure before-and-after conversion instead.

Q: What are the most common conversion problems on Indian D2C stores?
A: Slow mobile pages, product pages that leave buyer questions unanswered, unclear delivery time and COD availability, missing reviews, no reason to add a second item to the cart, and long checkouts. Most stores have three or four of these, and fixing them comes before any testing.

Q: Should I fix conversion before spending more on ads?
A: Usually, yes. Every improvement in conversion rate lowers cost per purchase across all channels at once, so a store that converts poorly wastes ad budget. We often run CRO and performance marketing together so that landing pages and ads are improved as one system.

Q: Do you change the design of my store?
A: Only where the evidence says to. CRO works within your brand and theme — reordering information, adding trust elements, simplifying steps — and is not a redesign. When a full redesign is the right answer, we say so and scope it separately.

Q: Which tools do you use for CRO?
A: GA4 for the funnel, Microsoft Clarity or Hotjar for heatmaps and recordings, Shopify or WooCommerce features and testing apps for experiments, and review platforms such as Judge.me for social proof. All are set up in your own accounts.


## D2C Performance Marketing
https://gaa-tha.com/services/d2c-performance-marketing
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha runs D2C performance marketing for Indian brands selling from their own store: Meta and Google shopping and catalogue ads, creative testing in batches, ROAS and MER targets set from contribution margin, attribution fixes such as Conversions API and checkout tracking, and email and WhatsApp retention flows so repeat orders lower your blended acquisition cost.

Best for: D2C brands in beauty, food, fashion, wellness and home with a live Shopify or WooCommerce store
Timeline: Setup in 2 weeks, then monthly
Engagement model: Monthly management fee; ad spend paid directly to Meta and Google
Channels/platforms: Meta, Google Shopping and Performance Max, YouTube, email, WhatsApp

### What it is
D2C performance marketing is paid and retention marketing for a brand that sells from its own website, run against profit-based targets: return on ad spend (ROAS) per channel and marketing efficiency ratio (MER) across the whole business. It covers Meta and Google shopping, catalogue and search ads, creative testing, tracking and attribution, and the email and WhatsApp flows that bring customers back for a second order.

gaa-tha starts with your unit economics — product margin, shipping, returns and payment costs — to set the ROAS and MER the account must hit, then fixes tracking so the numbers can be trusted. Creative is produced in-house in batches, budgets move weekly to what is working, and retention flows are built early because repeat orders are where D2C margin lives.

### What's included
- Unit-economics workshop to set ROAS, MER and cost-per-purchase targets
- Meta Pixel, Conversions API, Google Ads conversion tracking and GA4 checkout events verified
- Meta campaigns: Advantage+ shopping, catalogue and retargeting with product feeds
- Google Shopping, Performance Max, Search and YouTube campaigns with an optimised Merchant Center feed
- Creative testing framework: reels, statics, UGC and AI ad shoots tested in batches
- Offer and landing-page alignment with the CRO team
- Retention flows on email and WhatsApp: welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase, win-back
- Weekly budget, bid and audience optimisation with exclusions for existing customers where needed
- Monthly report on ROAS by channel, MER, new versus repeat revenue and contribution after ad spend

### How we work
1. Economics and targets — We work through margin, shipping, returns and payment costs to set the ROAS and MER the business can afford, per product line where they differ.
2. Tracking and feeds — Pixel, CAPI, Google conversion tracking, GA4 and the product feeds are fixed so every purchase is attributed and every product is eligible to show.
3. Creative and launch — The first creative batches and offers are produced, campaigns are structured for prospecting, retargeting and retention, and go live with daily checks.
4. Optimise weekly — Budgets follow performance, losing creative is retired, winning angles are extended, and retention flows are tuned on open and order rates.
5. Report monthly — ROAS by channel, MER, new versus repeat revenue and contribution after ad spend, with the scaling plan for next month.

### Deliverables
- Target sheet with ROAS, MER and cost-per-purchase by product line
- Verified tracking across Meta, Google Ads and GA4
- Optimised Merchant Center and Meta catalogue feeds
- Monthly creative batches with test results
- Email and WhatsApp retention flows
- Monthly performance report with contribution after ad spend

Tools & platforms: Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, Google Merchant Center, Google Analytics 4, Meta Conversions API, Klaviyo, WhatsApp Business API, Shopify
Pricing model: Monthly management retainer scoped to channels, spend and creative volume; ad spend is paid directly to Meta and Google from your own ad accounts with no markup, and email or WhatsApp tool charges are paid to the providers.

### FAQ
Q: What does D2C performance marketing include?
A: Meta and Google shopping, catalogue, search and video ads, creative testing, tracking and attribution fixes, and retention flows on email and WhatsApp — all reported against ROAS and MER targets set from your margins. gaa-tha runs it as one monthly retainer with the ad accounts in your name.

Q: What is the difference between ROAS and MER?
A: ROAS is revenue divided by ad spend for one channel or campaign, as reported by that platform. MER (marketing efficiency ratio) is total revenue divided by total marketing spend across every channel, taken from your store's own numbers. ROAS guides daily optimisation; MER tells you whether the business is actually profitable, because platforms tend to over-claim credit for the same order.

Q: What ROAS should a D2C brand target?
A: The one your margin allows, not a fixed number. A brand with high gross margin and low returns can profit at a lower ROAS than a low-margin brand with high COD returns. We calculate the break-even ROAS per product line first, then set targets above it so each order contributes after ad spend, shipping and returns.

Q: Why do my Meta and Shopify numbers not match?
A: Because Meta attributes orders on its own rules and windows, browsers block some tracking, and Google and Meta can both claim the same purchase. Fixing the Conversions API, checkout tracking and GA4 events closes most of the gap, and reporting on MER from store revenue gives you one number nobody can inflate.

Q: Do you also make the ad creatives?
A: Yes. Reels, UGC-style videos, AI ad shoots, statics and copy are produced in-house so testing does not wait on a separate agency. Creative is the biggest lever in performance today, and we plan batches monthly around the angles that are working.

Q: How much should I spend to start?
A: Enough to get statistically useful purchase data within two to three weeks, which for most Indian D2C brands means a daily budget sized from your average order value and target cost per purchase rather than a rule of thumb. We size it in the economics workshop and scale in steps once cost per purchase is stable.

Q: Do you handle email and WhatsApp retention too?
A: Yes. Welcome, abandoned-cart, post-purchase, replenishment and win-back flows on Klaviyo or a WhatsApp Business API provider are part of the retainer, because repeat orders are what make paid acquisition profitable.

Q: Can you run marketplace ads alongside D2C ads?
A: Yes. Amazon, Flipkart and quick-commerce ads are run by the same team with a shared view of budget across channels, so we can see where the next rupee earns the most.


## Ecommerce SEO
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ecommerce-seo
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha provides ecommerce SEO for Shopify and WooCommerce stores in India: keyword-mapped collection and product pages, Product, Review and Breadcrumb schema, technical fixes for crawl, speed and duplicate URLs, and blog clusters that feed your collections, so the store earns organic traffic on Google and gets cited in AI answers alongside paid ads.

Best for: Shopify and WooCommerce stores with 30+ products that want organic revenue to reduce ad dependence
Timeline: Audit and fixes in the first month; rankings build over 3–6 months
Engagement model: Monthly retainer; one-time audit available
Channels/platforms: Google Search, Google Shopping free listings, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity

### What it is
Ecommerce SEO is the practice of making an online store's collection, product and content pages rank in Google and appear in AI-generated answers, so the store earns traffic and orders without paying per click. It differs from general SEO because stores have hundreds of similar pages, faceted filters, variants and out-of-stock products, all of which create duplicate and thin pages that must be managed deliberately.

gaa-tha maps buying keywords to collections first — because a collection page for cold-pressed groundnut oil converts better than a blog about it — then fixes the technical layer, adds schema so Google and AI assistants can read price, availability and ratings, and builds blog clusters that link into those collections. Rankings are reported alongside organic revenue, not just positions.

### What's included
- Keyword research mapped to collections, sub-collections and product pages by buying intent
- Collection page copy, titles and descriptions written answer-first for Google and AI assistants
- Product page optimisation: titles, descriptions, alt text, variant and FAQ content
- Product, Offer, Review, Breadcrumb and Organization schema markup
- Technical SEO: crawl budget, faceted navigation, canonical tags, pagination, redirects and out-of-stock handling
- Site speed and Core Web Vitals fixes on mobile
- Internal linking from blog clusters to collections and from products to related collections
- Google Merchant Center free listings and Search Console monitoring
- Monthly report on rankings, organic sessions, organic revenue and AI citations

### How we work
1. Audit — Technical crawl, index coverage, current rankings, competitor collections and where organic revenue is coming from today.
2. Keyword map — Every target keyword is assigned to one collection, product or article so pages do not compete with each other.
3. Fix and build — Technical fixes, schema, collection copy and product page templates go live, with new collections created where demand exists.
4. Content clusters — Guides and comparisons are written around each priority collection and linked into it, giving Google and AI tools reasons to cite the store.
5. Track and expand — Monthly reporting on rankings and organic revenue, with the next collections and clusters chosen from the data.

### Deliverables
- Ecommerce SEO audit with prioritised technical fixes
- Keyword-to-page map for collections, products and content
- Optimised collection and product page copy and metadata
- Implemented schema markup validated in Search Console
- Monthly content cluster articles linked to collections
- Monthly ranking and organic revenue report

Tools & platforms: Google Search Console, Google Analytics 4, Google Merchant Center, Screaming Frog, Ahrefs, Semrush, Shopify, WooCommerce
Pricing model: Monthly retainer scoped to catalogue size, the number of priority collections and the content volume; a one-time audit with a fix list is available for stores that want to implement in-house.

### FAQ
Q: What is ecommerce SEO and how is it different from regular SEO?
A: Ecommerce SEO makes a store's collection and product pages rank and get cited, and it must handle problems ordinary websites do not have: hundreds of similar pages, filter URLs, variants, seasonal stock and product schema. Regular SEO focuses on a smaller set of service or content pages. gaa-tha runs ecommerce SEO for Shopify and WooCommerce stores as a monthly retainer.

Q: How long does ecommerce SEO take to show results?
A: Technical fixes and schema can change how pages appear within weeks, while new rankings for competitive collection keywords usually take three to six months to build. Stores with existing authority and a clean structure move faster; new domains take longer and benefit from running ads in the meantime.

Q: Should I optimise collection pages or write blogs?
A: Collections first. A collection page that ranks for a buying keyword sends visitors straight to products, while a blog post ranks for research keywords and needs a second step. Blogs come after, in clusters that link into the collections and give AI assistants a reason to cite you.

Q: What schema markup does an online store need?
A: Product and Offer schema with price, currency and availability, AggregateRating and Review where you have reviews, BreadcrumbList on every page and Organization on the site. Shopify themes add some by default but it is often incomplete or duplicated, so we validate every template in Search Console.

Q: How do you handle out-of-stock and discontinued products?
A: Temporarily out-of-stock products stay live with availability schema and a back-in-stock option, because deleting them loses rankings. Discontinued products are redirected to the closest replacement or the parent collection, never left as 404 pages.

Q: Can ecommerce SEO get my products into ChatGPT and AI Overviews?
A: It helps. AI assistants draw on pages that answer clearly, carry structured data and are cited elsewhere, so answer-first collection copy, complete schema, FAQs on product pages and consistent brand facts across the web all raise the chance of being recommended. We track AI citations as part of monthly reporting.

Q: Do you also run Google Shopping ads?
A: Yes, through our D2C performance marketing service. The same Merchant Center feed powers free listings and paid Shopping ads, so fixing the feed for SEO improves both.


## D2C Brand Launch
https://gaa-tha.com/services/d2c-brand-launch

Engagement model: Phased project fee; optional monthly growth retainer after launch
Channels/platforms: Shopify, Instagram, Meta ads, Google, WhatsApp, influencers; Amazon and quick commerce later

### What it is
A D2C brand launch is the end-to-end process of taking a product from concept to its first customers online: positioning and naming, brand identity and packaging, product photography and copy, an ecommerce store with payments and shipping, tracking, a launch campaign and the operating rhythm for the first weeks. Done as one project it avoids the usual gap where the brand agency finishes and the store and ads start from scratch.

gaa-tha runs launches for founders and for manufacturers moving from white-label or B2B supply into their own consumer brand. Strategy comes first — who the buyer is, what the product is for, why it costs what it costs — and every asset from the logo to the first reel is made against that. The Shopify store, Meta ads, influencer seeding and WhatsApp follow-ups are built by the same team, so launch day is a campaign, not a hope.

### What's included

- Product photography and AI ad shoots for store, marketplace and social use
- Shopify store design and development with checkout, shipping, COD rules and tracking

### FAQ
Q: What does a D2C brand launch package include?
A: Positioning, naming and brand identity, packaging, product photography, a Shopify store with payments, shipping and tracking, thirty days of launch content, a launch campaign across Meta ads, influencers and WhatsApp, and the first month of operations. gaa-tha delivers it as one phased project with one timeline.

Q: How long does it take to launch a D2C brand?
A: Eight to fourteen weeks from brief to first orders, if the product is ready. Branding and packaging take three to five weeks, the store and content run in parallel for four to six, and pre-launch and launch take two to three. Packaging print lead times and product readiness are the usual delays.

Q: Do I need branding before the store, or can I launch first and brand later?
A: Brand first, at least a minimum viable identity, because packaging, the store and every ad depend on it and redoing them later costs more than doing them once. The launch package is sequenced so the identity is locked before store design starts.

Q: Should I launch on Shopify or Amazon first?
A: Your own Shopify store first for margin, customer data and brand control, with Amazon and quick commerce added once the product, reviews and creative are proven. For some categories — commodity staples, impulse snacks — a marketplace or Blinkit listing can come sooner, and we advise by category.

Q: What do I need to have ready before we start?
A: A product that is formulated or manufactured, its cost and target price, any licences your category needs such as FSSAI for food or cosmetic registrations, GST registration and a bank account. Everything else — name, identity, packaging, store, content and campaign — is part of the package.

Q: How much budget should I keep for launch ads?
A: Separate from the project fee, keep a launch media budget for the first four to eight weeks that can buy enough purchase data to learn what converts; we size it from your unit economics in the strategy phase rather than quoting a fixed figure. Influencer fees and samples are budgeted alongside it.

Q: Can you keep running the brand after launch?
A: Yes. Most launches move into a monthly retainer covering store management, performance marketing, social content and, when ready, Amazon and quick-commerce onboarding, with the same team that built the brand.
