## Amazon Seller Onboarding
https://gaa-tha.com/services/amazon-onboarding
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha handles Amazon seller onboarding in India end to end: Seller Central registration, Brand Registry, category and restricted-category approvals, a clean catalogue with the right attributes, A+ content, a Brand Store and a go-live checklist covering pricing, FBA or Easy Ship and tax settings — so your first order arrives on a listing built to rank.

Best for: D2C, FMCG, home, beauty, fashion and manufacturers launching a retail brand on Amazon.in
Timeline: 2–4 weeks from documents to live listings; Brand Registry and gated categories can add time
Engagement model: One-time onboarding fee; optional monthly account management afterwards
Channels/platforms: Amazon.in Seller Central, Brand Registry, FBA, Easy Ship, Amazon Business

### What it is
Amazon seller onboarding is the process of setting a brand up to sell on Amazon.in: registering a Seller Central account with GST, PAN and bank details, enrolling the trademark in Brand Registry, getting approval for gated categories, creating listings with correct attributes and images, adding A+ content and a Brand Store, and choosing how orders will be fulfilled. Done properly it takes a few weeks; done badly it becomes months of suppressed listings and support cases.

At gaa-tha onboarding is treated as the foundation of a marketplace P&L rather than a form-filling exercise. We work out the fee, shipping and return economics per SKU before anything goes live, build the catalogue so it can be optimised and advertised later, and hand over an account you own — every credential, document and approval in your business's name, not ours.

### What's included
- Seller Central registration with GST, PAN, bank account and address verification
- Brand Registry enrolment using your registered or applied-for trademark
- Category and restricted-category (gated) approvals with the invoices and certificates Amazon asks for
- Catalogue creation: parent–child variations, attributes, bullets, backend search terms and images to Amazon's specifications
- A+ content modules and a Brand Store with a homepage and category pages
- Fulfilment setup: FBA shipment plan, Easy Ship or Self Ship, and shipping templates
- Pricing, MRP, HSN codes and tax settings checked SKU by SKU
- Go-live checklist: listing QC, Buy Box eligibility, a test order and return settings
- Handover document with logins, policies to watch and a 30-day post-launch plan

### How we work
1. Eligibility and documents — We check your GST, trademark status, category restrictions and product compliance, then share a documents checklist and the fee and margin picture for each SKU.
2. Registration and Brand Registry — The Seller Central account is registered and verified in your business's name, Brand Registry is filed, and gated-category applications go in with the right supporting paperwork.
3. Catalogue build — SKUs are structured into parent–child variations with complete attributes, keyword-led titles and bullets, backend search terms and images shot or retouched to Amazon's rules.
4. Content and store — A+ content modules and a Brand Store are designed and published so the listing tells the brand story and cross-sells the range from day one.
5. Go-live and handover — Fulfilment, pricing, tax and return settings are verified with a test order, listings go live, and you receive a handover pack plus a 30-day watch on suppressions, Buy Box and first reviews.

### Deliverables
- Verified Seller Central account registered in your business's name
- Brand Registry approval and any gated-category approvals
- Uploaded catalogue with variations, attributes, search terms and compliant images
- Published A+ content pages and Brand Store
- Fulfilment configuration (FBA, Easy Ship or Self Ship) with shipping templates
- Go-live checklist, handover document and 30-day post-launch plan

Tools & platforms: Amazon Seller Central, Amazon Brand Registry, A+ Content Manager, Amazon Stores builder, Fulfilment by Amazon (FBA), Amazon Easy Ship, Google Sheets
Pricing model: One-time onboarding fee scoped to SKU count, categories and content volume; Amazon's own referral, closing and fulfilment fees are paid by you to Amazon, and we share the current structure for your category before you start.

### FAQ
Q: What documents do I need to sell on Amazon India?
A: For most categories: a GST registration (regular scheme, not composition), PAN, a current bank account, identity and business address proof, and product details with MRP and HSN codes. Brand Registry needs a registered or applied-for trademark, and gated categories such as food, beauty or toys ask for invoices, FSSAI or BIS certificates. Requirements change, so gaa-tha shares a current checklist before you apply.

Q: How long does Amazon seller onboarding take?
A: Account verification usually takes a few days to a week once documents are correct. Catalogue, images and A+ content take one to three weeks depending on SKU count, and Brand Registry or gated-category approvals can run in parallel or add a week or two. Most brands we onboard are live within two to four weeks.

Q: What fees does Amazon charge sellers in India?
A: Amazon charges a referral fee by category, a closing fee by price band, shipping or FBA fulfilment fees, and storage fees if you use FBA; advertising is extra. The percentages vary by category and are revised from time to time, so we do not quote a number here — we share the current structure and model your net margin per SKU before listing.

Q: Do I need a trademark to sell on Amazon?
A: No, you can sell without one, but Brand Registry requires a registered or pending trademark and unlocks A+ content, a Brand Store, Sponsored Brands ads and protection against copycat listings. If you do not have one, we help you file through a trademark attorney and start listing while the application is pending.

Q: FBA or Easy Ship — which should I choose?
A: FBA suits fast-moving SKUs where the Prime badge and delivery speed drive conversion; Easy Ship suits bulky, fragile or slower SKUs shipped from your own warehouse; Self Ship rarely makes sense for a new seller. We model fees, returns and stock-holding per SKU and often recommend a mix.

Q: I already sell on Flipkart. Can you reuse that catalogue for Amazon?
A: Largely, yes. Product data, sizes and pricing carry over, but Amazon's attribute fields, image rules (a pure white background main image, product filling most of the frame) and title conventions differ, so we re-map and re-check everything rather than pasting it across.

Q: What happens once the listings go live?
A: The first 30 days are a watch period: we monitor suppressed listings, Buy Box status, first orders and early reviews, and fix anything Amazon flags. After that you can run the account yourself or move to our monthly Amazon account management.

Q: What if a listing is suppressed or the account is deactivated during onboarding?
A: The usual causes are mismatched documents, missing attributes, MRP or image violations, or a category that needs approval. We fix the root cause, respond through Account Health with the evidence Amazon wants, and keep GST, bank and trademark details consistent from the start so it rarely happens.


## Amazon Account Management
https://gaa-tha.com/services/amazon-account-management
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha runs Amazon account management for Indian brands as a monthly retainer: listing optimisation, Sponsored Products, Brands and Display ads, pricing and deals, inventory and FBA planning, account health, review and rating management, and a monthly P&L-style report that shows what you actually kept after Amazon's fees, ads and returns.

Best for: Brands already live on Amazon.in that want more orders without losing margin
Timeline: Audit in week one, then monthly with weekly optimisation
Engagement model: Monthly retainer; Amazon fees and ad spend paid directly to Amazon
Channels/platforms: Amazon.in, Amazon Ads, FBA, Amazon Business, Brand Analytics

### What it is
Amazon account management is the ongoing operation of a brand's Seller Central account: keeping listings optimised and unsuppressed, running Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display ads, planning prices, coupons and Lightning Deals, forecasting inventory and FBA shipments, protecting account health, managing reviews and reconciling payments against fees and returns. It is a weekly operating rhythm, not a one-time setup.

At gaa-tha every Amazon account is run by a named account manager against one number agreed with you — usually net margin after fees, ads and returns. Listings, ads and deals are decisions made in service of that number, and the monthly review shows sales, Amazon fees, ad spend, returns and what is left, SKU by SKU.

### What's included
- Listing audits and refreshes: titles, bullets, attributes, search terms, images and A+ content
- Amazon Ads management — Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display with weekly bid and budget work
- Pricing, coupons, Lightning Deals and event plans for Prime Day and the Great Indian Festival
- Inventory forecasting, FBA shipment plans and Inventory Performance Index (IPI) monitoring
- Account health: order defect rate, late shipment, policy violations and IP complaints handled as they appear
- Review and rating management using Amazon's own tools and policies
- Brand Store and A+ updates for new launches and seasons
- Payment reconciliation: settlements checked against orders, fees, returns and FBA reimbursement claims
- Weekly scorecard and monthly P&L-style report with next month's plan

### How we work
1. Audit and baseline — We review listings, ads, account health, inventory and the last three months of settlement reports, then agree the target number and the SKUs that matter most.
2. Fix the catalogue — Suppressed or weak listings are repaired first: attributes, images, A+ content and search terms, so ads and deals are not spent on pages that do not convert.
3. Ads and deals — Campaigns are restructured by product and intent, budgets set against ACoS and TACoS targets, and coupons, deals and event participation planned on a calendar.
4. Inventory and health — A rolling forecast drives FBA shipments and safety stock; account health metrics are watched weekly and issues answered before they become suspensions.
5. Report and review — A weekly scorecard keeps the team honest; the monthly review shows sales, fees, ads, returns and net margin per SKU, and sets the plan for the next month.

### Deliverables
- Weekly scorecard: orders, revenue, ACoS/TACoS, rank, stock cover and account health
- Ads campaign structure and a running optimisation log
- Deals and promotions calendar for the quarter
- Inventory forecast and FBA shipment plan
- Settlement reconciliation sheet with reimbursement claims filed
- Monthly P&L-style report with next month's actions

Tools & platforms: Amazon Seller Central, Amazon Ads console, Amazon Brand Analytics, Fulfilment by Amazon (FBA), Helium 10, Google Sheets, Looker Studio
Pricing model: Monthly retainer scoped to SKU count, ad spend and the work involved; Amazon's fees and advertising costs are paid by you directly to Amazon, with no markup from us.

### FAQ
Q: What does an Amazon account management agency do?
A: It runs your Seller Central account day to day: listing content and A+ updates, advertising, pricing and deals, inventory and FBA shipments, account health, reviews, payment reconciliation and reporting. gaa-tha does this on a monthly retainer with a named account manager, and you keep full ownership of the account.

Q: How do you keep my products in stock on FBA?
A: With a rolling forecast built from sell-through, lead times and upcoming events, translated into FBA shipment plans and safety stock per SKU. We watch the Inventory Performance Index and ageing stock so storage fees do not creep up, and flag stock-outs before they cost rank.

Q: Do you also handle Amazon Vendor Central purchase orders?
A: Yes, where a brand sells to Amazon as a vendor. We confirm purchase orders, coordinate shipments and shipment notices, track fill rate, and dispute chargebacks and shortage claims, alongside the seller-side work if you run both.

Q: How do you decide prices, coupons and deals?
A: From a margin floor per SKU that accounts for referral, closing, fulfilment and return costs. Coupons, Lightning Deals and event pricing are planned to hit rank and volume goals without going below that floor, and we track whether a deal actually produced incremental sales.

Q: What is a good ACoS on Amazon India?
A: It depends on your gross margin and what the ad is for: a launch campaign can run at a higher ACoS to build rank and reviews, while a mature SKU should sit well inside its margin. We set targets per campaign and report TACoS (total ad spend against total sales) so growth in organic sales is visible.

Q: How do you handle negative reviews and low ratings?
A: Within Amazon's policies: automated review requests through Seller Central, Amazon Vine for eligible new products, prompt replies to buyer messages, and fixes to the product, packaging or listing when the same complaint keeps appearing. We never buy reviews or offer incentives for them.

Q: Do you reconcile Amazon payments and claim reimbursements?
A: Yes. Settlement reports are matched to orders, fees, refunds and returns every cycle, and we file claims for lost, damaged or unreturned FBA inventory. Missed reimbursements are one of the most common leaks in an Amazon account.

Q: What is in the monthly review?
A: A P&L-style view — sales, Amazon fees, ad spend, returns and net margin — by SKU, plus organic rank for target keywords, conversion rate, account health, stock cover and rating trend. It ends with the plan for the next month: what we will launch, cut, reprice or advertise.


## Flipkart Onboarding & Account Management
https://gaa-tha.com/services/flipkart-seller-management
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha manages Flipkart seller onboarding and account management for Indian brands: Seller Hub registration, catalogue and listing QC, Flipkart Ads (PLA and PCA), Big Billion Days and sale-event participation, pricing and offers, account health, returns and SPF claims, and monthly reporting — so the platform that reaches tier-2 and value-conscious buyers is run properly, not just switched on.

Best for: Fashion, home, kitchen, electronics accessories, FMCG and value-led D2C brands
Timeline: Onboarding in 2–3 weeks; account management monthly
Engagement model: One-time onboarding fee, then a monthly retainer; ad spend paid directly to Flipkart
Channels/platforms: Flipkart Seller Hub, Flipkart Ads, Flipkart Fulfilment (FBF), Shopsy

### What it is
Flipkart seller management is the work of registering a brand on Flipkart Seller Hub and then running the account every week: catalogue and listing quality checks, pricing and offers, Flipkart Ads (Product Listing Ads and Product Contextual Ads), participation in sale events such as Big Billion Days and Big Saving Days, account health metrics, returns, and Seller Protection Fund claims for damaged, wrong or missing returns. Flipkart rewards sellers who keep listings clean, prices sharp and service metrics green.

At gaa-tha Flipkart is run as its own channel with its own economics rather than a copy of the Amazon account. Buyers on Flipkart are more price-led and more likely to come from tier-2 and tier-3 cities, returns behave differently, and the sale-event calendar drives a larger share of the year, so the assortment, pricing ladder and ad plan are built for that.

### What's included
- Seller Hub registration, brand approval and category listing permissions
- Catalogue creation to Flipkart's attribute and image templates, with QC-rejection fixes
- Listing optimisation: titles, key features, descriptions and search-relevant attributes
- Flipkart Ads management — Product Listing Ads (PLA) and Product Contextual Ads (PCA) with weekly optimisation
- Sale-event planning and nominations for Big Billion Days, Big Saving Days and category events
- Pricing, discounts, Flipkart coupons and offer participation against a margin floor
- Fulfilment setup: Flipkart Fulfilment (FBF) or seller-fulfilled, with Flipkart Assured eligibility work
- Account health: cancellation, returns, breach and seller-rating metrics tracked weekly
- Returns handling and Seller Protection Fund (SPF) claims with evidence
- Shopsy cross-listing for price-led SKUs and a monthly performance report

### How we work
1. Eligibility and setup — We confirm GST, bank, brand and category requirements, register the Seller Hub account in your business's name and secure brand and category approvals.
2. Catalogue and QC — SKUs are built to Flipkart's templates with complete attributes and compliant images, and every QC rejection is fixed until the catalogue is fully live.
3. Pricing and fulfilment — A pricing ladder is set against fees and return costs, fulfilment is configured through FBF or your own warehouse, and Flipkart Assured eligibility is worked towards.
4. Ads and events — PLA and PCA campaigns are launched by product and keyword, and sale events are planned months ahead with stock, pricing and ad budgets.
5. Operate and report — Weekly work on listings, ads, account health, returns and SPF claims, with a monthly report on orders, revenue, ad efficiency, returns and net margin.

### Deliverables
- Verified Flipkart Seller Hub account with brand and category approvals
- Fully live catalogue with QC issues cleared
- PLA and PCA campaign structure with a weekly optimisation log
- Sale-event calendar with stock, pricing and ad plans
- Returns and SPF claims tracker
- Monthly performance report by SKU

Tools & platforms: Flipkart Seller Hub, Flipkart Ads, Flipkart Fulfilment (FBF), Shopsy, Google Sheets, Looker Studio
Pricing model: One-time onboarding fee scoped to SKU count, then a monthly management retainer; Flipkart's commission, fixed, collection and shipping fees and your ad spend are paid directly to Flipkart, and we share the current structure before you begin.

### FAQ
Q: What documents do I need to sell on Flipkart?
A: GST registration, PAN, a current bank account with a cancelled cheque, identity and business address proof, and product details with MRP and HSN. Brand-owned listings usually need a trademark certificate or a brand authorisation letter, and categories like food or cosmetics need their licences. gaa-tha shares the current checklist before you apply.

Q: How long does Flipkart onboarding take?
A: Registration and verification usually take a few days, and the catalogue takes one to two weeks depending on SKU count and how many QC rounds are needed. Most brands are live within two to three weeks, with the first sale-event nomination planned straight after.

Q: What fees does Flipkart charge?
A: A commission by category, a fixed fee by order value, a collection fee and shipping fees, plus optional FBF storage and advertising. The rates vary by category and price band and are revised periodically, so we share the current structure and model your net margin per SKU before listing.

Q: What is the difference between PLA and PCA on Flipkart Ads?
A: Product Listing Ads (PLA) show your products in search results and product pages against keywords or categories and are paid per click; Product Contextual Ads (PCA) are banner placements on Flipkart's pages, better for brand visibility and event pushes. Most brands start with PLA and add PCA around sale events.

Q: How do we prepare for Big Billion Days?
A: Nominations, pricing and stock are usually locked weeks before the event, so we plan two to three months out: which SKUs go into the event, the discount ladder, FBF inbound dates, ad budgets and creative. During the event, ads and prices are watched daily.

Q: How do you handle returns and SPF claims?
A: Returns are checked against reasons and images, and every wrong, damaged or missing return that qualifies is filed as a Seller Protection Fund claim with the evidence Flipkart asks for within the deadline. A claims tracker shows what was filed, approved and paid.

Q: Is Flipkart Assured worth it?
A: Usually, yes: the badge signals quality and reliable delivery, and buyers filter for it. Eligibility depends on fulfilment through FBF or meeting service metrics, packaging standards and quality checks, so we work towards it as part of onboarding.

Q: Should I also list on Shopsy?
A: If your SKUs work at low ticket sizes, yes — Shopsy is Flipkart's price-led app and listings can be extended from the same Seller Hub account. We select SKUs where the margin still holds after Shopsy's fee structure and returns.


## Myntra Onboarding & Management
https://gaa-tha.com/services/myntra-onboarding
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha handles Myntra onboarding and management for fashion, footwear, accessories and beauty brands: eligibility review against Myntra's curated brand criteria, registration on the Myntra Partner Portal, a style-level catalogue with fit, fabric and occasion attributes, model imagery to Myntra's specs, Myntra Ads, and a calendar built around End of Reason Sale and Big Fashion Festival.

Best for: Apparel, footwear, bags, jewellery, watches and beauty brands with a trademark and a real range
Timeline: Eligibility and approval 2–6 weeks; catalogue and go-live 2–4 weeks after approval
Engagement model: One-time onboarding fee; optional monthly management retainer
Channels/platforms: Myntra Partner Portal, Myntra Ads, Myntra Studio content, EORS and Big Fashion Festival

### What it is
Myntra onboarding is the process of getting a fashion or beauty brand approved and live on Myntra, India's largest fashion marketplace: passing Myntra's brand curation, agreeing a commercial model, registering on the Myntra Partner Portal, building a style-level catalogue where every colour and size sits under one style with fit, fabric, pattern and occasion attributes, and supplying model imagery that meets Myntra's portrait image standards. Unlike Amazon or Flipkart, Myntra chooses its brands, so eligibility comes before everything else.

At gaa-tha we treat Myntra as a fashion buyer, not a listing form. Myntra's shoppers browse by look, filter by fit and occasion, and buy heavily during sale events, so we build the pitch, the assortment and the catalogue around how the platform merchandises — and manage the account afterwards with ads, event nominations, returns analysis and monthly sell-through reviews.

### What's included
- Eligibility review: trademark, category fit, assortment depth, pricing band and returns readiness against Myntra's curation
- Brand pitch deck and registration on the Myntra Partner Portal, with the commercial model explained before you sign
- Style-level catalogue: article type, gender, fit, fabric, pattern, sleeve, neck, occasion, wash care, country of origin and size chart per style
- Image production or QC to Myntra's portrait specs — front, back, side and detail shots on a plain background, no text or watermarks
- Size charts and measurement tables built to reduce size-related returns
- Pricing and discount ladder that survives Myntra's event discounting
- Myntra Ads setup: sponsored listings and placements by style and category
- Event calendar and nominations for End of Reason Sale, Big Fashion Festival and category days
- Ongoing management: stock sync, order and returns monitoring, ratings, new-style launches and monthly review

### How we work
1. Eligibility review — We check trademark status, category, assortment size, price band, packaging and returns readiness against what Myntra's category teams look for, and tell you honestly whether to apply now or build first.
2. Pitch and registration — A short brand deck and the registration on the Myntra Partner Portal go in together, the commercial model on offer is walked through with you, and agreements and bank details are completed.
3. Catalogue and imagery — Every style is set up with its colour and size options, full fashion attributes and a size chart; images are shot or checked to Myntra's portrait standards so listings pass QC first time.
4. Pricing, ads and events — A discount ladder is agreed for regular and event periods, Myntra Ads are set up for hero styles, and the first End of Reason Sale or Big Fashion Festival nomination is planned.
5. Go-live and management — Listings go live with a QC pass, and the account moves to a monthly rhythm: stock, orders, returns, ratings, new drops and a sell-through review by style.

### Deliverables
- Eligibility report and brand pitch deck
- Registered Myntra Partner Portal account and completed agreements
- Style-level catalogue with attributes, size charts and QC-passed images
- Pricing ladder for regular and event periods
- Myntra Ads setup and event calendar for the season
- Monthly sell-through, returns and ratings review by style

Tools & platforms: Myntra Partner Portal, Myntra Ads, Myntra Studio, Adobe Photoshop, Google Sheets, Looker Studio
Pricing model: One-time onboarding fee scoped to style count and imagery needs, then an optional monthly management retainer; Myntra's commission and logistics charges vary by category and commercial model and are shared with you before you sign.

### FAQ
Q: Is Myntra open to any seller?
A: No. Myntra curates its brands, so a new label is reviewed for trademark ownership, category fit, range depth, pricing and the ability to handle fashion returns before it is accepted. gaa-tha runs this eligibility review first and, where a brand is not ready, tells you what to build before applying.

Q: What documents do I need to sell on Myntra?
A: A registered trademark or trademark application with a brand authorisation letter, GST registration, PAN, a current bank account, a signed agreement, and product details with MRP, HSN, country of origin and size charts. Beauty brands also need product compliance documents. The checklist changes, so we share the current version at the start.

Q: How long does Myntra onboarding take?
A: Approval typically takes two to six weeks because a category team reviews the brand; the catalogue and image QC then take two to four weeks depending on how many styles you launch with. Timing an application so you are live before End of Reason Sale or Big Fashion Festival matters more than the exact number of days.

Q: What are Myntra's commission and other charges?
A: Myntra charges a commission by category plus logistics and other charges, and the numbers depend on the commercial model you are offered — marketplace-style, just-in-time or outright purchase. They vary and change, so we do not quote figures; we walk you through the current structure and model margin per style before you sign.

Q: What are Myntra's image requirements?
A: Portrait-format images with the garment on a model against a plain, light background; front, back, side and detail views; consistent framing across the range; and no text, logos, props or watermarks on the image. Footwear, bags and beauty have their own angle sets. We either shoot to these specs or QC and retouch your existing images.

Q: How does Myntra handle returns and will they hurt me?
A: Fashion returns on Myntra are high by nature and are usually deducted from settlements, so sizing accuracy, honest imagery and packaging matter more than on other platforms. We build proper size charts, analyse return reasons by style each month and drop or fix styles that keep coming back.

Q: Which sale events matter on Myntra?
A: End of Reason Sale (EORS), which runs more than once a year, and Big Fashion Festival in the run-up to Diwali are the two that move volume, along with category and payday events. Nominations, stock and discounts are locked well in advance, so we plan the calendar a season ahead.

Q: Can you also run Nykaa Fashion and AJIO alongside Myntra?
A: Yes. The three platforms have different curation, catalogue templates, image standards and event calendars, so we run them as separate accounts from one team, with a shared assortment and pricing plan so you are not undercutting yourself.

gaa-tha manages Nykaa and Nykaa Fashion onboarding for beauty, personal care, wellness and fashion brands: eligibility review, brand and product-compliance documentation, registration, an ingredient- and claim-checked catalogue for Nykaa or a style-level catalogue for Nykaa Fashion, images to each platform's specs, ad placements and an event calendar built around Pink Friday and Hot Pink Sale.

At gaa-tha we run the two platforms as two different jobs. Nykaa buyers research ingredients, shade and skin type and trust expert-style content, so the beauty catalogue is built around claims that can be substantiated and images that show the product, its label and its texture. Nykaa Fashion buyers shop premium and occasion-led styles, so that catalogue follows fashion attributes and portrait model imagery. Both get an event calendar and ad plan built for Nykaa's audience.

### What's included
- Eligibility review: brand positioning, price band, category fit and compliance readiness for Nykaa or Nykaa Fashion
- Compliance file: cosmetics manufacturing licence, ingredient (INCI) lists, shelf life, batch and expiry, legal metrology label checks and claim substantiation
- Brand pitch and registration, with the commercial model on offer explained before you sign
- Nykaa catalogue: product type, concern, skin or hair type, key ingredients, benefits, how to use, shade or variant mapping and size or volume
- Nykaa Fashion catalogue: style-level listings with fit, fabric, occasion, care and size charts

- Pricing and offer ladder for regular periods and Nykaa's sale events
- Ad placements: sponsored product listings, category banners and sampling with orders, planned with Nykaa's ad team
- Event calendar and nominations for Pink Friday Sale, Hot Pink Sale and category campaigns, plus ongoing management

### How we work
1. Eligibility and compliance — We review positioning, pricing and category fit, then assemble the compliance file — licences, ingredient lists, shelf life, labels and claims — so the application does not stall on paperwork.
2. Pitch and registration — A short brand deck and registration go to the relevant Nykaa or Nykaa Fashion category team, and the commercial model and agreement are walked through with you before signature.
3. Catalogue and imagery — Beauty SKUs are written around ingredients, concerns and usage with shade and variant mapping; fashion styles are built with full attributes and size charts. Images are shot or QC'd to each platform's specification.
4. Pricing, ads and events — An offer ladder is set for regular and event periods, ad placements and sampling are planned for hero SKUs, and the first Pink Friday or Hot Pink Sale nomination is scheduled.
5. Go-live and management — Listings go live after QC, and the account moves to a monthly rhythm: stock, orders, ratings and reviews, new launches, campaign participation and a sell-through review by SKU.

### Deliverables
- Eligibility report and compliance file ready for submission
- Registered account and completed agreements on Nykaa or Nykaa Fashion
- Approved catalogue with ingredient, claim and attribute data and QC-passed images
- Offer ladder for regular and event periods
- Ad placement and sampling plan with an event calendar for the season
- Monthly review of sell-through, ratings and campaign results

Tools & platforms: Nykaa seller tools, Nykaa Fashion seller tools, Nykaa ad placements, Adobe Photoshop, Google Sheets, Looker Studio
Pricing model: One-time onboarding fee scoped to SKU count, compliance work and imagery, then an optional monthly management retainer; Nykaa's margins, marketing contributions and logistics charges vary by category and model and are shared with you before you sign.

### FAQ
Q: Can any beauty brand sell on Nykaa?
A: No. Nykaa curates its brands and expects a clear positioning, a sensible price band, and full product compliance before it lists you. gaa-tha runs an eligibility review first and tells you what to fix — usually labels, claims or ingredient documentation — before the application goes in.

Q: What documents does Nykaa ask for?
A: Typically a trademark certificate or authorisation letter, GST, PAN and bank details, a cosmetics manufacturing licence or importer registration, ingredient lists, shelf-life and batch details, product images including the back label, and proof for any claims such as dermatologically tested. Nykaa Fashion asks for brand and business documents and size charts instead of product compliance. We share the current checklist at the start.

Q: How long does Nykaa onboarding take?
A: Approval by a category team typically takes three to eight weeks because compliance is checked, and the catalogue and image QC take another two to four weeks. Nykaa Fashion is usually quicker. We time applications so you are live before Pink Friday or a Hot Pink Sale rather than during one.

Q: What does Nykaa charge sellers?
A: Nykaa works on margins or commissions by category, with logistics charges and sometimes marketing contributions, and the structure depends on the commercial model you are offered. The numbers vary and change, so we do not publish them; we walk you through the current terms and model your margin per SKU before you sign.

Q: What are Nykaa's image requirements?
A: For beauty: square, white-background product images with the product filling most of the frame, a legible back-label image, texture or swatch shots, and shade charts for colour cosmetics; no text overlays or watermarks. For Nykaa Fashion: portrait model imagery with front, back and detail views on a plain background. We shoot or retouch to these specs so listings pass QC.

Q: What is the difference between Nykaa and Nykaa Fashion for a brand?
A: Nykaa is the beauty, personal-care and wellness platform; Nykaa Fashion is a separate curated fashion and lifestyle platform with its own category teams, catalogue templates, image standards and events. A brand with both beauty and fashion lines is onboarded on each separately, and we manage them as two accounts with one plan.

Q: Which Nykaa sale events matter?
A: The Pink Friday Sale around the Black Friday period and the Hot Pink Sale are the biggest, alongside category campaigns and festive events. Nominations, stock and offers are locked in advance, so we plan the calendar a season ahead and prepare content for each campaign.

Q: Do you also handle Nykaa reviews and ratings?
A: Yes, as part of ongoing management: replies to reviews and questions, monitoring of shade and skin-type complaints that signal a listing problem, and product fixes when the same feedback repeats. We work within Nykaa's policies and never buy or incentivise reviews.


## AJIO Onboarding
https://gaa-tha.com/services/ajio-onboarding
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha handles AJIO onboarding for fashion, footwear and lifestyle brands: eligibility review against AJIO's brand-led curation, seller registration and agreement, a style-level catalogue mapped to AJIO's attribute and size templates, model imagery to AJIO's specs, sponsored placements and a calendar built around AJIO's Big Bold Sale and All Stars Sale, with ongoing management if you want it.

Best for: Apparel, footwear, ethnic wear, bags and lifestyle labels, including homegrown and premium brands

### What it is
AJIO onboarding is the process of getting a fashion or lifestyle brand approved and live on AJIO, the fashion marketplace owned by Reliance Retail: passing its brand curation, agreeing a commercial model, registering as a seller, building a style-level catalogue to AJIO's attribute and size templates, and supplying imagery that meets its standards. AJIO also runs AJIO Luxe for premium and designer labels, AJIOGRAM for homegrown and independent brands, and AJIO Business for wholesale buyers, so which door you enter through matters.

At gaa-tha we position the brand for the right part of AJIO before applying. AJIO's audience skews towards ethnic and occasion wear, homegrown labels and value-conscious fashion buyers across metros and smaller cities, and its sale calendar — Big Bold Sale, All Stars Sale and festive events — carries a large share of the year, so assortment, pricing and stock planning are built around it from the start.

### What's included
- Eligibility review: trademark, category, range depth, price band and which AJIO programme fits (AJIO, AJIO Luxe, AJIOGRAM or AJIO Business)
- Brand pitch, seller registration and agreement, with the commercial model explained before you sign
- Style-level catalogue mapped to AJIO's templates: article type, gender, fit, fabric, pattern, occasion, care, country of origin and size chart
- Image production or QC to AJIO's specs — model shots on a clean background, consistent framing, front, back and detail views, no text or watermarks
- Size charts and measurement tables for apparel and footwear to cut size-related returns
- Pricing and discount ladder for regular and event periods
- Sponsored placements and campaign participation planned with AJIO's category team
- Event calendar and nominations for Big Bold Sale, All Stars Sale and festive campaigns
- Ongoing management: stock, orders, returns, ratings, new-style launches and monthly review

### How we work
1. Eligibility and programme fit — We check trademark, category, range and pricing, and recommend whether AJIO, AJIO Luxe, AJIOGRAM or AJIO Business is the right entry point — or whether to build the range first.
2. Pitch and registration — A brand deck and seller registration go to AJIO's category team, and the commercial model, agreement and bank and GST details are completed with you.
3. Catalogue and imagery — Every style is built to AJIO's attribute and size templates with a size chart, and imagery is shot or QC'd to AJIO's standards so listings pass the first time.
4. Pricing, placements and events — A discount ladder is agreed for regular and event periods, sponsored placements are planned for hero styles, and the first Big Bold Sale or All Stars Sale nomination is scheduled with stock.
5. Go-live and management — Listings go live after QC, and the account moves to a monthly rhythm: stock and orders, returns analysis by style, ratings, new drops and a sell-through review.

### Deliverables
- Eligibility report with programme recommendation and brand pitch deck
- Registered AJIO seller account and completed agreements
- Style-level catalogue with attributes, size charts and QC-passed images
- Pricing ladder for regular and event periods
- Placement plan and event calendar for the season
- Monthly sell-through, returns and ratings review by style

Tools & platforms: AJIO seller tools, AJIO sponsored placements, Adobe Photoshop, Google Sheets, Looker Studio
Pricing model: One-time onboarding fee scoped to style count and imagery, then an optional monthly management retainer; AJIO's commission, logistics and marketing charges vary by category and commercial model and are shared with you before you sign.

### FAQ
Q: Is AJIO open to new brands?
A: AJIO is curated, but it actively looks for homegrown and independent labels through AJIOGRAM and premium labels through AJIO Luxe, alongside its main marketplace. A brand needs a trademark, a coherent range and pricing that fits its audience. gaa-tha reviews eligibility and recommends the right programme before applying.

Q: What documents do I need to sell on AJIO?
A: GST registration, PAN, a current bank account, a trademark certificate or brand authorisation letter, business address proof, a signed seller agreement, and product data with MRP, HSN, country of origin and size charts. Requirements vary by programme and change, so we share the current checklist at the start.

Q: How long does AJIO onboarding take?
A: Brand review and approval typically take two to six weeks, followed by two to three weeks for catalogue build and image QC. We time the application so the brand is live and stocked before Big Bold Sale or All Stars Sale rather than trying to join mid-event.

Q: What does AJIO charge sellers?
A: A commission by category plus logistics and marketing charges, with the structure depending on the commercial model you are offered. The figures vary and are revised, so we do not quote them; we explain the current terms and model your margin per style before you sign.

Q: What are AJIO's image requirements?
A: Model imagery on a clean, consistent background with front, back and detail views, a fixed framing across the range, and no text, logos or watermarks on the image; footwear and bags follow their own angle sets. We shoot or retouch to these specs, and reuse of Myntra imagery is usually possible after a check against AJIO's template.

Q: What is AJIO Business and should I use it?
A: AJIO Business is Reliance's wholesale platform for retailers and resellers buying in bulk. It suits manufacturers and labels that want B2B volume alongside, or instead of, consumer sales. We assess whether the margin and MOQ structure works for you and can onboard both sides.

Q: Which AJIO sale events matter?
A: Big Bold Sale and All Stars Sale are the largest, along with festive and payday events. Nominations, stock and discounts are locked in advance, so we plan the calendar a season ahead and prepare pricing and stock for each.

Q: Should I launch on AJIO or Myntra first?
A: Myntra usually first for reach, unless your range is ethnic, occasion or value-led, where AJIO's audience is a strong fit and its curation can be more open to homegrown labels. Many brands run both; we plan a shared assortment and pricing so the two accounts do not undercut each other.


## Meesho, JioMart & Other Marketplaces
https://gaa-tha.com/services/meesho-jiomart-onboarding
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha handles onboarding and management for Meesho, JioMart and India's other marketplaces — Shopsy, Snapdeal and Tata CLiQ — for brands that want price-led mass reach beyond Amazon and Flipkart: registration, catalogue built for each platform's format, pricing that survives low ticket sizes and high returns, platform promotions, and a monthly view of what each channel actually earns.

Best for: Apparel, home, kitchen, FMCG, grocery and general merchandise brands with value price points
Timeline: Registration in a few days; catalogue and go-live in 1–3 weeks per platform
Engagement model: One-time onboarding fee per platform; optional monthly management retainer
Channels/platforms: Meesho Supplier Panel, JioMart Seller Center, Shopsy, Snapdeal, Tata CLiQ

### What it is
Meesho and JioMart onboarding is the process of registering a brand on India's price-led and mass-reach marketplaces and building catalogues that work there: Meesho for low-ticket fashion, home and lifestyle bought by value-conscious and reseller audiences in smaller cities, JioMart for grocery, FMCG and general merchandise under Reliance, and Shopsy, Snapdeal and Tata CLiQ for their own audiences. Each has its own seller panel, catalogue format, fee structure and return behaviour.

At gaa-tha these platforms are approached with a clear view of the economics. Low ticket sizes, cash-on-delivery, returns and shipping can turn a busy channel into a loss-making one, so we choose which SKUs go on which platform, price them for the net margin rather than the headline, and report each channel separately every month so you can scale the ones that pay.

### What's included
- Platform selection: which of Meesho, JioMart, Shopsy, Snapdeal and Tata CLiQ suits your category and price points
- Registration on the Meesho Supplier Panel, JioMart Seller Center and other seller portals, with brand approvals where needed
- Catalogue creation to each platform's template, including bulk uploads and category-specific attributes
- Price and pack-size planning against fees, shipping, cash-on-delivery and return costs per platform
- Platform promotions and event participation, such as Meesho's Mega Blockbuster Sale and JioMart's festive sales
- Order, RTO (return to origin) and returns monitoring with claims filed where the platform allows
- Ratings, catalogue quality scores and account health tracked weekly
- Monthly per-channel report on orders, revenue, returns and net margin

### How we work
1. Channel and SKU selection — We map your range and price points to each platform's buyer and fee structure, and choose the SKUs that can make money on Meesho, JioMart and the others.
2. Registration and approvals — Seller accounts are registered in your business's name on each platform, with GST, bank, brand and category approvals completed and documented.
3. Catalogue build — Listings are built to each platform's template — bulk uploads, category attributes, image rules and pack-size variants — and QC rejections are fixed until everything is live.
4. Pricing and promotions — Prices are set from a net-margin model per platform, and promotions and sale-event participation are planned for the SKUs where the margin holds.
5. Operate and report — Orders, RTO, returns, ratings and account health are watched weekly, and a monthly per-channel report shows what each marketplace is really earning.

### Deliverables
- Platform and SKU recommendation with a per-platform margin model
- Registered seller accounts with approvals, in your business's name
- Live catalogues on each chosen platform
- Pricing and promotions plan per platform
- Returns and RTO tracker with claims log
- Monthly per-channel performance report

Tools & platforms: Meesho Supplier Panel, JioMart Seller Center, Shopsy, Snapdeal Seller Panel, Tata CLiQ seller tools, Google Sheets
Pricing model: One-time onboarding fee per platform scoped to SKU count, then an optional monthly management retainer; each platform's commission, shipping and other charges are paid directly to that platform, and we share the current structure before you begin.

### FAQ
Q: What documents do I need to sell on Meesho or JioMart?
A: Usually GST registration, PAN, a current bank account, identity and address proof, and product details with MRP and HSN; brands need a trademark or authorisation letter for branded listings, and food and grocery SKUs on JioMart need FSSAI. Meesho has at times allowed sellers without GST in specific categories, so we confirm the current rules for your category before you apply.

Q: How long does onboarding on Meesho or JioMart take?
A: Registration and verification usually take a few days on each platform, and the catalogue goes live within one to three weeks depending on SKU count and QC rounds. Running several platforms in parallel does not add much time because the product data is prepared once and re-mapped.

Q: What do Meesho and JioMart charge?
A: Each platform has its own structure — commission by category, shipping charges, payment or collection fees, and penalties for returns or cancellations — and Meesho's model is known for being commission-light while shipping and returns carry more of the cost. Rates vary and change, so we share the current structure per platform and model your net margin before listing.

Q: Is Meesho worth it for a brand, or only for resellers?
A: It depends on your price points. Meesho reaches a very large value-conscious audience in smaller cities, but low ticket sizes, cash-on-delivery and returns squeeze margin. It works for brands with SKUs designed for that price band; we select those SKUs rather than putting the whole range on.

Q: Which of these marketplaces should I start with?
A: JioMart for grocery, FMCG and household; Meesho and Shopsy for value fashion, home and lifestyle; Tata CLiQ for mid-premium fashion and electronics; Snapdeal for value general merchandise. We recommend an order based on your category and margin, usually after Amazon and Flipkart are live.

Q: How do you handle returns and RTO on these platforms?
A: By tracking return reasons and RTO rates by SKU and pincode, filing claims where the platform allows for wrong or damaged returns, and adjusting pricing, packaging or the assortment where a SKU keeps coming back. Returns are the biggest hidden cost on price-led marketplaces, so they are reviewed every month.

Q: What happens after go-live?
A: You can run the accounts yourself with the handover document, or move to our monthly management, which covers promotions, ratings, returns, catalogue quality and a per-channel report. Many brands keep management on the two or three platforms that prove profitable and pause the rest.


## Fashion & Licensed-Merch Marketplace Growth
https://gaa-tha.com/services/fashion-marketplace-growth
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha builds growth plans for fashion and licensed-merchandise brands across Myntra, Flipkart, Nykaa Fashion, AJIO and Amazon: which styles go where, platform-specific content and imagery, a pricing and discount ladder that keeps margin through sale events, sponsored ads per platform, and monthly reviews of sell-through, returns and rank — one plan instead of five disconnected seller accounts.

Best for: Apparel, footwear and accessory labels, and brands selling licensed character, film, sports, anime or music merchandise
Timeline: Growth plan in 2–3 weeks, then a monthly retainer across platforms
Engagement model: Monthly retainer scoped to platforms and style count; ad spend paid directly to each platform
Channels/platforms: Myntra, Flipkart, Nykaa Fashion, AJIO, Amazon Fashion, Shopsy

### What it is
Fashion marketplace growth is the practice of running a fashion or licensed-merchandise brand across several marketplaces as one business: deciding the assortment each platform gets, producing content and imagery to each platform's standard, setting a pricing and discount ladder that holds through End of Reason Sale, Big Billion Days and festive events, running sponsored ads per platform, and reviewing sell-through, returns and rank by style every month. For licensed merchandise it also covers licensor approvals, IP paperwork and drop calendars tied to releases.

At gaa-tha the plan starts with the style sheet and the margin, not the platform. A hero style may deserve model imagery and ads on Myntra, a value variant may belong on Flipkart and Shopsy, and a limited licensed drop may need a launch date, artwork approvals and stock held back for one platform's event. We run the accounts so these decisions are made deliberately and reviewed monthly.

### What's included
- Assortment plan: which styles, colours and price points go on Myntra, Flipkart, Nykaa Fashion, AJIO and Amazon
- Platform-specific content: titles, attributes, size charts and imagery to each platform's template
- Pricing and discount ladder for regular, event and end-of-season periods, with a margin floor per style
- Sale-event calendar across platforms: End of Reason Sale, Big Fashion Festival, Big Billion Days, Big Bold Sale, Pink Friday and festive events
- Sponsored ads per platform for hero styles and new drops, managed weekly
- Licensed-merch workflow: licensor artwork and listing approvals, authorisation letters for marketplace IP checks, royalty-ready sales reporting
- Drop planning for licensed releases and seasonal collections, with stock allocation by platform
- Returns analysis by style and size, with fixes to size charts, imagery and packaging
- Monthly sell-through, rank, returns and net-margin review by style and platform

### How we work
1. Range and margin review — We go through the style sheet, costs, current platform performance and, for licensed brands, the licence terms and approval process, and agree the number the plan is run against.
2. Assortment and pricing plan — Each style is assigned to the platforms where it can sell at margin, with a discount ladder that survives event pricing and a stock allocation by platform.
3. Content and catalogue — Listings, attributes, size charts and imagery are produced or fixed to each platform's standard, and licensed artwork and listings are cleared with the licensor before upload.
4. Ads, events and drops — Sponsored ads are set up per platform for hero styles, sale-event nominations are planned a season ahead, and licensed drops are scheduled around release dates.
5. Review and rebalance — Every month we review sell-through, returns, rank and net margin by style and platform, then move stock, budget and discounting to what is working.

### Deliverables
- Assortment and platform allocation plan by style
- Pricing and discount ladder with margin floors
- Cross-platform sale-event and drop calendar for the season
- Platform-ready catalogues and imagery
- Licensor approval log and authorisation documents for marketplaces
- Monthly sell-through, returns and net-margin review by style and platform

Tools & platforms: Myntra Partner Portal, Flipkart Seller Hub, Amazon Seller Central, Nykaa Fashion seller tools, AJIO seller tools, Google Sheets, Looker Studio
Pricing model: Monthly retainer scoped to the number of platforms, styles and ad accounts; platform commissions and ad spend are paid by you directly to each marketplace, and we share each platform's current structure before you commit.

### FAQ
Q: What is a fashion marketplace growth plan?
A: It is a single plan for selling a fashion range across Myntra, Flipkart, Nykaa Fashion, AJIO and Amazon: which styles go where, how each is priced and discounted through the year, what content and imagery each platform gets, how much ad budget each hero style receives, and how sell-through and returns are reviewed. gaa-tha builds it and then runs the accounts against it.

Q: Should a fashion brand be on every marketplace?
A: Usually not with the whole range. Each platform has a different buyer, fee structure and return behaviour, so a style that makes money on Myntra can lose money on a value platform. We put each style where the margin holds and keep a shared pricing ladder so platforms do not undercut each other.

Q: How do you handle licensed merchandise on marketplaces?
A: Marketplaces check IP ownership, so listings need the licensor's authorisation letter and approved artwork, and licensors usually need to sign off on product images, listing copy and sometimes pricing. We run the approval workflow, keep the paperwork ready for brand-registry and IP checks, and produce sales reports in the format royalty statements need.

Q: How do you keep margin through sale events?
A: With a discount ladder set in advance: a regular price, an event price and an end-of-season floor per style, each checked against fees, returns and cost. Styles that cannot meet the floor at event pricing are held out of the event or given limited stock rather than discounted into a loss.

Q: How do you reduce fashion returns?
A: By analysing return reasons by style and size every month and fixing the cause: accurate size charts and measurement tables, honest colour and fabric imagery, fit notes in the listing, and packaging that arrives well. Styles with persistently high returns are repriced or dropped from the platforms where they are returned most.

Q: Do you plan drops for licensed releases and collections?
A: Yes. Licensed drops are scheduled around film, series, sports or music release dates with artwork cleared in advance, stock allocated to the platforms where the audience is, and ads and event placements booked for launch week. Seasonal collections follow the same drop calendar.

Q: Can you also run our own website alongside the marketplaces?
A: Yes. Many fashion brands keep exclusive styles or full-price launches on their Shopify store and use marketplaces for reach, and we plan the two together so pricing and stock make sense across both. Our D2C ecommerce team handles the store and performance marketing.


## Marketplace Listing & Catalogue Optimisation
https://gaa-tha.com/services/marketplace-listing-optimisation
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha optimises marketplace listings and catalogues for Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa, AJIO, Meesho and JioMart: keyword research per platform, titles, bullets and descriptions written for the search algorithm and the buyer, complete attributes and backend keywords, image stacks and A+ modules, competitor benchmarking, and tracking of rank and conversion so you can see which change did what.

Best for: Brands with live listings that get traffic but not sales, or rank below competitors for their own category keywords
Timeline: Audit in week one; optimisation in 2–4 weeks depending on SKU count; then quarterly refreshes
Engagement model: Project fee per catalogue, or included in a monthly account management retainer
Channels/platforms: Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa, AJIO, Meesho, JioMart

### What it is
Marketplace listing optimisation, often called marketplace SEO, is the work of making a product listing rank higher in a marketplace's search results and convert more of the shoppers who see it: researching the keywords buyers use on that platform, writing titles, bullets and descriptions around them, filling every attribute so the listing appears in filters, adding backend search terms, building an image stack that answers the buyer's questions, and adding A+ or rich content where the platform supports it. Each marketplace has its own algorithm, so the same product is optimised differently on Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra.

At gaa-tha optimisation is measured, not assumed. We benchmark the listing against the top competitors for its keywords, change the elements most likely to move rank and conversion first, and track organic rank, click-through, conversion and sales for each SKU before and after so the effect of the work is visible in the monthly report.

### What's included
- Listing audit against each platform's ranking factors and the top competitors for your keywords
- Keyword research per platform using search-term data, autocomplete and competitor listings
- Titles, bullets, key features and descriptions rewritten for search relevance and readability
- Attribute completion so listings appear in filters: size, material, colour, fit, concern, pack size and more
- Backend search terms and platform-specific fields such as Amazon's search terms and Flipkart's key features
- Image stack planning: main image to spec, lifestyle, infographic, size, texture and packaging shots
- A+ content and rich-content modules with comparison tables and brand story
- Variation and parent–child structure fixes so reviews and rank are consolidated
- Rank and conversion tracking by SKU with a before-and-after report

### How we work
1. Audit and benchmark — Every SKU is scored against the platform's ranking factors and compared with the top listings for its keywords, and the SKUs with the most to gain are prioritised.
2. Keyword research — Search terms are gathered per platform from search data, autocomplete, competitor listings and category browse paths, then mapped to each SKU by intent.
3. Copy and attributes — Titles, bullets, descriptions, attributes and backend keywords are rewritten to the platform's rules, with variations structured so rank and reviews consolidate.
4. Images and A+ content — The image stack is planned and produced or retouched, and A+ or rich-content modules are designed to answer objections and cross-sell.
5. Upload, track and refresh — Changes go live in batches, rank and conversion are tracked by SKU, and the listing is refreshed each quarter or when the algorithm, competitors or season change.

### Deliverables
- Listing audit and competitor benchmark per SKU
- Keyword map by platform and SKU
- Optimised titles, bullets, descriptions, attributes and backend keywords, uploaded
- Image stack briefs and finished images to platform specs
- A+ and rich-content modules, published
- Before-and-after rank and conversion report

Tools & platforms: Amazon Seller Central, Amazon Brand Analytics, Helium 10, Flipkart Seller Hub, Myntra Partner Portal, Adobe Photoshop, Google Sheets
Pricing model: Project fee scoped to the number of SKUs, platforms and images, or included in a monthly marketplace management retainer; no platform fees are charged through us.

### FAQ
Q: What is marketplace listing optimisation?
A: It is the process of improving a product listing so it ranks higher in a marketplace's search and converts more visitors: keywords, titles, bullets, descriptions, attributes, backend search terms, images and A+ content, all written to that platform's algorithm and buyer. gaa-tha does this per platform and tracks rank and conversion by SKU to prove the change worked.

Q: How is marketplace SEO different from Google SEO?
A: Marketplace algorithms rank on relevance plus performance — conversion rate, sales velocity, price, availability and reviews — rather than on backlinks and site authority. Keywords still matter, but a listing that converts poorly will not hold rank however well it is written, so images, price and reviews are part of the work.

Q: My listings get views but few orders. What is usually wrong?
A: Most often the main image, price relative to the competitors shown next to it, missing reviews, or an image stack that does not answer size, material or usage questions. The audit tells us which, and we fix conversion before spending on ads to send more traffic to the same page.

Q: Do you do keyword research separately for each platform?
A: Yes. Buyers search differently on Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra, and each platform exposes different data — Amazon's search-term reports, Flipkart's category and key-feature fields, Myntra's attribute filters. A keyword map is built per platform and SKU rather than copied across.

Q: Is A+ content worth it?
A: For branded products with a story, comparisons or usage to explain, usually yes: it improves conversion and lets you cross-sell the range. It matters less for commodity SKUs where price and delivery decide. On Amazon it needs Brand Registry, which we can set up.

Q: Do you create the product images too?
A: Yes. Our product photography and AI ad-shoot teams produce main images to platform spec, lifestyle and infographic images, and size or texture shots, or we retouch your existing images to pass QC and convert better.

Q: How soon do optimised listings show results?
A: Rank and conversion typically start moving within two to four weeks of changes going live, as the platform re-indexes the listing and gathers new performance data. Competitive keywords take longer and usually need ads and reviews alongside the copy work.


## Marketplace Ads Management
https://gaa-tha.com/services/marketplace-ads-management
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha manages marketplace advertising on Amazon (Sponsored Products, Brands and Display), Flipkart (PLA and PCA), Myntra, Nykaa and AJIO: campaign structure by product and intent, keyword and placement harvesting, bid and budget management every week, event-period plans for Prime Day, Big Billion Days and End of Reason Sale, and reporting on ACoS, TACoS and organic rank.

Best for: Brands with optimised listings and stock in place, ready to buy rank and volume profitably
Timeline: Setup in 1–2 weeks, then monthly with weekly optimisation
Engagement model: Monthly management fee; ad spend paid directly to each platform
Channels/platforms: Amazon Ads, Flipkart Ads, Myntra Ads, Nykaa ad placements, AJIO sponsored placements

### What it is
Marketplace ads management is the ongoing work of running paid placements inside marketplaces — Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display on Amazon, Product Listing Ads and Product Contextual Ads on Flipkart, and sponsored listings and banners on Myntra, Nykaa and AJIO — so that products win search positions and category placements at a cost that fits the margin. It covers campaign structure, keyword and placement selection, bids, budgets, negatives, event-period pushes and reporting on ACoS, TACoS and the organic rank the ads help build.

At gaa-tha marketplace ads are run against the unit economics of each SKU rather than a single account-wide target. Launch SKUs are allowed a higher cost of sale to earn rank and reviews; mature SKUs are held inside their margin; event periods get their own budgets and bid rules. Ad spend stays in your own ad accounts and is reported alongside organic sales so you can see whether the ads are growing the business or just replacing sales you already had.

### What's included
- Ad account audit or setup on Amazon Ads, Flipkart Ads, Myntra Ads and Nykaa or AJIO placements
- Campaign architecture by product, match type and intent: branded, category, competitor and defensive
- Keyword and placement harvesting from search-term reports, with negatives to cut waste
- Weekly bid, budget and placement optimisation against per-SKU ACoS and TACoS targets
- Sponsored Brands and Display creative, including brand-store and video placements where available
- Event-period plans and budgets for Prime Day, Great Indian Festival, Big Billion Days, End of Reason Sale and platform sale events
- Coordination with listing, pricing, stock and reviews so ads are not sent to pages that cannot convert
- Monthly report on spend, sales, ACoS, TACoS, organic rank movement and new-to-brand customers

### How we work
1. Audit and targets — We review current campaigns, listings, margins and stock, then set ACoS and TACoS targets per SKU group — launch, growth and mature — instead of one number for the account.
2. Structure and keywords — Campaigns are rebuilt by product and intent, keywords and placements are chosen from search-term and competitor data, and negatives are set from day one.
3. Launch and learn — Campaigns go live with daily checks in the first two weeks to catch runaway spend, then bids and budgets are moved to the terms and placements that convert.
4. Events and scale — Event budgets, bid rules and creative are planned ahead of Prime Day, Big Billion Days and End of Reason Sale, and winners are scaled with rank as the check.
5. Report and refine — A monthly report shows spend, sales, ACoS, TACoS, organic rank and cannibalisation by SKU, and sets the next month's budget and tests.

### Deliverables
- Campaign architecture document and naming conventions per platform
- Keyword and placement map with negatives, updated monthly
- Weekly optimisation log
- Event-period budget and bid plan for each sale event
- Sponsored Brands and Display creative assets
- Monthly ads report on ACoS, TACoS and organic rank by SKU

Tools & platforms: Amazon Ads console, Amazon Brand Analytics, Flipkart Ads, Myntra Ads, Helium 10, Google Sheets, Looker Studio
Pricing model: Monthly management fee scoped to platforms and spend; ad spend is paid by you directly to each marketplace from your own ad accounts, with no markup.

### FAQ
Q: What does a marketplace ads agency do?
A: It runs paid placements inside marketplaces — Amazon Sponsored Products, Brands and Display, Flipkart PLA and PCA, and sponsored listings and banners on Myntra, Nykaa and AJIO — from campaign structure and keyword selection to weekly bid work, event budgets and reporting. gaa-tha does this on a monthly fee with the ad accounts owned by you.

Q: What is the difference between ACoS and TACoS?
A: ACoS is ad spend divided by the sales those ads produced; TACoS is ad spend divided by total sales including organic. ACoS tells you whether a campaign is efficient; TACoS tells you whether ads are growing the whole business or just replacing organic sales. We report both and manage to TACoS over time.

Q: How much should I spend on marketplace ads?
A: Enough to gather useful data on each SKU group within a few weeks and to defend your own brand terms, sized from your margin and the target cost of sale rather than a fixed rule. Launch SKUs need more relative to sales; mature SKUs should need less as organic rank builds. We set a starting budget per platform and adjust monthly.

Q: Should I run ads before my listings are optimised?
A: No. Ads send traffic to the listing, so a weak main image, incomplete attributes, no reviews or an uncompetitive price wastes the spend. We fix the listing and pricing first or in parallel, then scale ads once conversion is sound.

Q: How do you plan ads for Prime Day, Big Billion Days or End of Reason Sale?
A: With a separate event plan: higher budgets and bid ceilings for the days that matter, creative and deals aligned, stock confirmed, and daily monitoring during the event. Budgets are wound down after the event so the account does not keep bidding at event levels.

Q: Do you run Flipkart and Myntra ads as well as Amazon?
A: Yes. Flipkart PLA and PCA, Myntra Ads and Nykaa and AJIO placements each have their own tools and rules, and we run them from one team with a shared view of budget and results, so spend goes to the platform where each SKU converts best.

Q: Do I keep the ad accounts and the data?
A: Yes. Every ad account is created in your business's name or accessed through your existing seller account, spend is billed to you by the platform, and all campaign history stays with you if we stop working together.


## Reviews & Ratings Management
https://gaa-tha.com/services/reviews-ratings-management
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha manages reviews and ratings on Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa and other marketplaces the policy-compliant way: review requests through each platform's tools, Amazon Vine where it fits, packaging inserts that stay within the rules, response templates for negative reviews, root-cause fixes for recurring complaints, and a rating recovery plan for listings that have slipped below the level buyers trust.

Best for: New listings with no reviews, and established listings whose rating has dropped or whose negative reviews go unanswered
Timeline: Setup in 1–2 weeks; review velocity builds over 2–3 months; then ongoing
Engagement model: Monthly retainer, standalone or as part of account management
Channels/platforms: Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa, AJIO, JioMart, Google Business Profile

### What it is
Reviews and ratings management is the work of earning more genuine reviews for a product, responding to the ones it gets, and recovering a rating that has fallen — all within the marketplace's policies. It includes review requests through the platform's own tools, programmes such as Amazon Vine, compliant packaging inserts, response templates and service-level targets for negative reviews and buyer questions, analysis of complaint themes, and fixes to the product, packaging or listing that remove the cause. Buying reviews, incentivising positive reviews or asking only happy customers to review are policy violations that put the whole account at risk, so none of that is part of it.

At gaa-tha reviews are treated as a signal about the product and the listing, not only as a number to push up. Every negative review is tagged by cause — size, damage in transit, expectation set by the listing, quality — and the monthly review shows which causes are growing so the fix goes into the product or the page rather than into more requests.

### What's included
- Review audit: rating, review count, velocity and complaint themes by SKU against competitors
- Automated review requests through Seller Central and each platform's equivalent, timed to delivery
- Amazon Vine enrolment for eligible new products and other platform review programmes where available
- Policy-compliant packaging inserts and thank-you cards that ask for honest feedback without incentives
- Response templates and a service-level target for negative reviews, ratings and buyer questions
- Complaint-theme analysis with fixes to size charts, imagery, packaging or product
- Reporting of reviews that breach platform guidelines through the proper channels
- Rating recovery plan for listings below the rating buyers filter for, including variation and relaunch options
- Monthly report on rating, review count, velocity and complaint themes by SKU

### How we work
1. Audit and targets — We review rating, velocity and complaint themes for every SKU, compare them with competitors, and agree which listings need volume, which need recovery and which need a product fix.
2. Compliant request system — Platform review requests are switched on and timed, Vine or equivalent programmes are enrolled where eligible, and inserts are designed to stay inside the rules.
3. Response process — Templates, tone and a response-time target are set for negative reviews and buyer questions, so no complaint sits unanswered on the page.
4. Fix the causes — Complaints are tagged by cause each week and the recurring ones are fixed at the source — listing expectations, size charts, packaging or the product itself.
5. Recover and report — Listings below the trusted rating get a recovery plan, and the monthly report shows rating, velocity and complaint trends by SKU.

### Deliverables
- Review audit and per-SKU targets
- Configured review-request system and Vine or programme enrolments
- Compliant packaging insert designs
- Response templates and service-level guide
- Complaint-theme tracker with fixes logged
- Monthly ratings and reviews report

Tools & platforms: Amazon Seller Central, Amazon Vine, Flipkart Seller Hub, Myntra Partner Portal, Nykaa seller tools, Google Business Profile, Google Sheets
Pricing model: Monthly retainer scoped to the number of SKUs and platforms, standalone or bundled into account management; programme fees such as Amazon Vine are paid by you directly to the platform.

### FAQ
Q: Can you get me more reviews on Amazon or Flipkart?
A: Yes, within the rules: review requests through the platform's own tools timed to delivery, Amazon Vine for eligible new products, and compliant inserts that ask for honest feedback. What we will not do is buy reviews, offer incentives or steer only happy customers to review, because that risks listing removal or account suspension.

Q: Is Amazon Vine worth it?
A: For a new product with few reviews, usually yes: Vine sends units to trusted reviewers who leave honest reviews quickly, which helps conversion and ads. It has an enrolment fee paid to Amazon and needs Brand Registry, so we use it for launches where early reviews change the outcome.

Q: How do you respond to negative reviews?
A: Quickly, publicly where the platform allows and always calmly: acknowledge the issue, state what has been done or offer a route to resolve it, and never argue. Buyer questions get the same treatment. A response target is agreed at the start so nothing sits unanswered.

Q: Can bad reviews be removed?
A: Only if they breach the platform's guidelines — for example, they are about delivery rather than the product, contain abuse, or are clearly for a different item. We report those through the proper channels with evidence. Genuine negative reviews cannot be removed; they are answered and their cause is fixed.

Q: How do you recover a listing whose rating has dropped?
A: First by finding the cause in the review themes and fixing it, then by rebuilding velocity with compliant requests so newer, better reviews shift the average. Where a product has changed materially, a new variation or relaunch is sometimes the honest route. Recovery usually takes two to three months.

Q: Do packaging inserts get sellers into trouble?
A: They can if they offer a reward, ask for a positive review or push buyers to review outside the platform. A neutral card that thanks the buyer, gives care or usage tips and asks for honest feedback is allowed on most platforms. We design inserts to those rules and review them when policies change.

Q: Which platforms do you cover?
A: Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa, AJIO and JioMart, plus Google Business Profile reviews for brands with stores or a local presence. Each has its own tools and policies, so the request and response process is set up per platform.


# Quick Commerce
https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce

Get into the 10-minute basket — and stay in stock there.

Quick Commerce is the gaa-tha practice for brands selling on India's 10-minute delivery platforms: Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket. We handle platform and city prioritisation, onboarding and documentation, catalogue and thumbnails, dark-store availability and fill rate, purchase-order coordination, quick-commerce ads and ratings — as one monthly operation.

## FAQ
Q: What is quick commerce and which platforms matter in India?
A: Quick commerce (q-commerce) is delivery of groceries, FMCG, beauty and everyday items in roughly 10–30 minutes from local dark stores. In India the platforms that matter are Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket (BB Now).

Q: What does a quick commerce agency do?
A: A quick commerce agency gets a brand listed on q-commerce platforms and then runs the account: catalogue and images, city and dark-store availability, purchase orders and replenishment, promotions and ads, ratings and monthly reporting. gaa-tha does this for all major Indian platforms from one team.

Q: Which quick commerce platform should I launch on first?
A: Start where your category and cities overlap best. Blinkit and Zepto lead in metro grocery and FMCG; Swiggy Instamart adds strong food and impulse categories; BigBasket suits staples and larger packs. We map your SKUs and target cities against each platform's category demand before recommending an order.

Q: What documents do I need to sell on Blinkit or Zepto?
A: Typically GST registration, brand ownership proof or an authorisation letter, bank details, product and pack-size data, and category licences such as FSSAI for food. Requirements change by platform and category, so we share a current checklist before you apply.

Q: Are there fees to get listed on quick commerce platforms?
A: Platforms work on margins, listing or onboarding charges and sometimes marketing contributions, and these vary by category and change over time. We share the current structure for your category before you sign anything, and plan pack sizes and pricing so the margin works.


## Quick Commerce Management
https://gaa-tha.com/services/quick-commerce-agency
Last updated: 2026-09-25

gaa-tha is a quick commerce agency in India that gets brands listed and selling on Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket — platform and city prioritisation, margin and pack-size planning, onboarding, catalogue and thumbnails, dark-store availability, purchase-order coordination, quick-commerce ads and ratings, run as one monthly operation with one report.

Best for: FMCG, food and beverage, beauty and personal care, baby and pet care, home and kitchen brands
