# FAQ — ecommerce, marketplaces, quick commerce and case studies
https://gaa-tha.com/faq


## Ecommerce, Marketplaces & Quick Commerce
Q: What is quick commerce and which platforms matter in India?
A: Quick commerce (q-commerce) is the delivery of groceries, FMCG, beauty and everyday products in roughly 10–30 minutes from local dark stores. In India the platforms that matter are Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket (BB Now). gaa-tha onboards brands onto all of them and runs the catalogue, availability, ads and ratings as one operation.

Q: What does a quick commerce agency do?
A: A quick commerce agency gets a brand listed on 10-minute delivery platforms and then runs the account: catalogue and thumbnails, city and dark-store availability, purchase orders and replenishment, promotions and ads, ratings and monthly reporting. We do this for Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket from one team, with one monthly report.

Q: Which quick commerce platform should I launch on first?
A: Start where your category and your target cities overlap best. Blinkit and Zepto lead metro grocery and FMCG; Swiggy Instamart is strong on food and impulse categories; BigBasket suits staples and larger packs; Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now are expanding city by city. We map your SKUs, margins and cities against each platform's category demand and recommend an order before you apply anywhere.

Q: How long does Blinkit, Zepto or Instamart onboarding take?
A: Typically two to six weeks from application to first purchase order, depending on category approvals, documentation and how quickly catalogue and images are ready. Food and beauty categories with licence checks take longer than packaged non-food. We prepare the documents, catalogue and images in parallel so the platform review is the only wait.

Q: What documents do I need to sell on Blinkit or Zepto?
A: Usually GST registration, brand ownership proof or a brand authorisation letter, bank account details, a trademark certificate or application where available, and category licences such as FSSAI for food. Product data — barcodes, MRP, pack sizes, shelf life, dimensions — is needed for the catalogue. Requirements change by platform and category, so we share a current checklist before you apply.

Q: Are there fees to get listed on quick commerce platforms?
A: Platforms work on a margin per SKU and may have onboarding, listing or marketing contributions; these vary by category and change over time, and some are negotiable at scale. We share the current structure for your category before you sign and plan pack sizes and pricing so the margin works after platform costs.

Q: What is marketplace account management?
A: Marketplace account management is the ongoing operation of a brand's seller account on platforms like Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and Nykaa: listings and A+ content, pricing and deals, sponsored ads, inventory and fulfilment planning, account health, reviews and monthly reporting. gaa-tha runs it as a monthly retainer with a named account manager and a P&L-style report.

Q: Do you handle Amazon and Flipkart onboarding?
A: Yes. Seller registration, Brand Registry or brand approval, category approvals, catalogue creation, A+ content, Brand Store and a go-live checklist — then optional monthly account management. Fashion and beauty brands can add Myntra, Nykaa and AJIO; price-led categories can add Meesho and JioMart.

Q: Can you manage D2C, marketplaces and quick commerce together?
A: Yes — that is the point of the practice. One team handles your Shopify store, Amazon and Flipkart accounts and Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart listings, so pricing, pack sizes, content and promotions stay consistent across every channel. You get one monthly report showing revenue and margin by channel rather than three agencies with three versions of the truth.

Q: Do you build and manage Shopify stores?
A: Yes. We design and develop Shopify stores — custom themes and sections, checkout and payment integrations, COD and pincode rules, Meta Pixel and Conversions API, GA4 — and run monthly store management for product uploads, price changes, banners, apps and fixes. Migrations from Amazon or WooCommerce are included in scope where needed.

Q: Can one website serve multiple store locations or franchises?
A: Yes. A multi-location Shopify build lets the customer enter a pincode or choose an outlet; the order is routed to that outlet with a WhatsApp notification, and each outlet can have its own availability, delivery rules and prepaid/COD settings on one shared catalogue and price list. It suits retail chains, franchises, sweet and snack stores and local delivery brands.

Q: How do you price ecommerce and quick commerce services?
A: Onboarding is a one-time project fee per platform. Ongoing work — account management, store management, ads — is a monthly retainer scoped to the number of platforms, SKUs and cities. Ad spend is paid by you directly to the platform, with no markup. We send a written scope and price within 48 hours of the first call.

Q: How do you measure success on marketplaces?
A: Orders, revenue and net margin after fees and returns; advertising ACoS/TACoS; organic rank for target keywords; conversion rate; ratings and review count; and account health. On quick commerce we add availability and fill rate by city. All of it is reported monthly against the targets agreed at the start.

Q: My listings are live but not selling — can you fix that?
A: Usually. Stalled listings almost always have one of four problems: weak titles and images, no reviews, uncompetitive pricing, or no advertising. We audit the account, fix content and pricing, set up sponsored ads and a compliant review process, and track rank and conversion weekly. If the problem is availability — out of stock or not live in the right cities — we fix that first.

Q: Do you create product images and A+ content?
A: Yes. White-background packshots, lifestyle scenes, infographic 'why buy' images, pack-size visuals and A+ or enhanced-content modules, made to each platform's specs — with AI-assisted shoots for large catalogues so 200-SKU ranges do not take months. Quick-commerce thumbnails are treated as their own format: they have to win in a two-second scroll.

Q: Do you make cinema ads?
A: Yes. Trailer-grade 10, 20 and 30-second films cut for cinema screens, OTT, YouTube and in-store displays — produced live-action or with AI and human art direction, delivered in 2.39:1 scope and vertical versions. They work best for retail chains, FMCG launches and festive campaigns that need city-wide recall.

Q: Do you generate B2B and export leads for manufacturers?
A: Yes. LinkedIn outreach to named decision-makers, Meta and LinkedIn lead ads, IndiaMART and TradeIndia listing optimisation, WhatsApp first-reply templates and a lead-qualification SOP with a tracker your sales team will actually use. It is built for manufacturers, exporters, packaging, machinery and bulk food suppliers.

## Case studies & results
Q: Can we see results from similar brands?
A: Yes. Our case studies are published one by one as each client approves them and the numbers are confirmed from real reports — we do not publish estimates. Browse what is live on the work page, and ask us for a walkthrough of unpublished work in your category on a call. Every case study lists the services used and links to those service pages.

Q: Do you work with manufacturers, FMCG, retail, real estate and education brands?
A: Yes. Current and past clients include packaged-snack and FMCG brands, sweets and gifting retailers, machinery, coatings and packaging manufacturers, a co-living brand, an overseas-education consultancy and a D2C skincare brand. The process is the same across industries; the channels and references change.

Q: Do you work with international clients?

## General FAQ
Q: What is marketing, in simple terms?
A: Marketing is the work of understanding what people want, building something worth wanting, and making sure the right people know about it at the moment they care. Advertising is only the visible tip of it.A complete marketing function covers five things: research (who is the customer and what do they actually need), positioning (why you and not the alternative), product and pricing, distribution (where they can buy), and promotion (how they hear about you). Businesses that treat marketing as only the last item tend to pay more for worse results.

Q: What is a marketing strategy?
A: A marketing strategy is the set of choices about who you serve, what you stand for, and how you will reach them — written down before any campaign starts. It answers four questions: which segment, what promise, which channels, and what success looks like in numbers.A strategy is not a list of posts or a content calendar. Those are tactics. Strategy is what makes the tactics agree with each other.

Q: How do I do better marketing?
A: Start by narrowing rather than broadening: pick one clear audience, one sharp promise, and two channels you can do properly instead of six you do badly. Then build a feedback loop — measure one primary metric per campaign, and change one variable at a time.The biggest practical gains for most Indian SMEs come from four moves: fix your positioning, make your offer concrete, publish content that answers real customer questions, and follow up leads faster.

Q: What's the difference between digital marketing and traditional marketing?
A: Traditional marketing buys attention in physical or broadcast spaces — print, hoardings, radio, TV — and measures reach by estimate. Digital marketing reaches people through search, social, email and web, and measures behaviour directly: who clicked, who bought, at what cost.The practical difference is feedback speed. Digital lets you test a message for a few thousand rupees and know within days whether it works. Most brands today use both, with digital carrying measurement and traditional carrying credibility.

Q: How much should a business spend on marketing?
A: A common working range is 5-10% of revenue for established businesses and 15-20% for brands in a growth or launch phase — but the more useful question is what a customer is worth to you. If a customer is worth ₹10,000 in lifetime profit, a ₹1,500 acquisition cost is excellent and a ₹12,000 one is fatal.Start by calculating customer lifetime value and target cost per acquisition. Budget follows those two numbers, not a percentage rule of thumb.

Q: How do I measure whether marketing is working?
A: Pick one primary metric per objective. For awareness, use reach and branded search volume. For consideration, use engagement rate, time on page and returning visitors. For revenue, use qualified leads, cost per acquisition and return on ad spend.Vanity metrics — follower counts, impressions, likes in isolation — tell you a post did something, not that the business grew. Track them as diagnostics, never as goals.

Q: What is branding, and how is it different from marketing?
A: Branding is the work of deciding what your business means to people — the name, the look, the voice, the promise. Marketing is the work of getting that meaning in front of the right audience and turning attention into revenue.Branding builds memory; marketing builds momentum. Get the order wrong and you spend money making people notice something they immediately forget.

Q: What is graphic design?
A: Graphic design is the craft of arranging type, image, colour and space so that information is understood and felt in the way it was intended. It is visual problem-solving, not decoration — a good design makes a message clearer, faster and more trustworthy.In practice it spans identity design (logos, brand systems), packaging, editorial and layout, advertising creative, motion graphics and digital interface design.

Q: What is the current form of graphic design in 2026?
A: Graphic design today is systems-first and motion-native. Designers are increasingly asked to deliver a flexible kit — type scale, colour tokens, component rules, motion behaviour — rather than a single static artwork, because the same identity has to work on a phone screen, a package, a reel and an AI-generated ad variant.The second shift is AI as a production tool. Generative tools now handle variation, resizing and rough concepting, which moves the designer's value up the stack: art direction, taste, brand judgement and knowing what not to make.

Q: What makes a good logo?
A: A good logo is distinctive, legible at every size, and honest about what the business is. The practical test: it must survive a 16-pixel favicon and a forty-foot hoarding, work in one colour, and still look unmistakably like you.A logo is a signature, not the whole brand. Colour, type, tone of voice and consistency do most of the recognition work over time.

Q: How much does a brand identity cost in India?
A: For small businesses and startups in India, a basic logo package typically runs from a few thousand rupees to around ₹50,000, while a full identity system — naming support, logo, colour and type system, applications and guidelines — generally starts around ₹50,000 and rises with scope.The variable is depth, not drawing time: strategy, research, application design and documentation are where most of the cost and most of the long-term value sit. gaa-tha scopes identity work to the business stage rather than a fixed price list.

Q: How do I choose a digital marketing agency in India?
A: Judge an agency on four things: relevant proof (work in a comparable category, with outcomes not just visuals), clarity of process, who actually does the work day to day, and how they report results. Ask for a client you can call.The most common red flags are guaranteed rankings, undisclosed ad-spend markups, and a pitch deck full of impressions but no revenue.

Q: What are AI ads and AI ad shoots?
A: AI ads are advertising creatives generated or enhanced with generative AI — product visuals, cinematic scenes, voiceovers and edits produced without a full traditional shoot. An AI ad shoot recreates the output of a physical production (models, locations, lighting, camera moves) using AI, at a fraction of the cost and turnaround.We combine both with human art direction so the result looks premium, never robotic.

Q: What is AI cloning — and is it safe for my brand?
A: AI cloning creates a licensed digital twin of a founder or spokesperson — voice and face — so you can produce unlimited spokesperson videos without booking a studio every time. It's done with full written consent, watermark-safe workflows and brand approval on every output.It's how founders stay on camera daily without shooting daily.

Q: Will AI-made ads look cheap or robotic?
A: Not when they're art-directed. Raw AI output does look generic — that's why every gaa-tha AI ad passes through human creative direction: brand-matched grading, typography, sound design and story structure. Our clients' AI ads have outperformed their traditional creatives on cost-per-result while looking richer.

Q: How much cheaper is an AI ad shoot than a traditional shoot?
A: Typically 60-90% cheaper. A traditional product or model shoot in India runs ₹1-10 lakh and up once you count crew, location, models and post-production. An AI ad shoot removes most of those line items and compresses weeks into days.High-stakes hero films may still warrant a hybrid: real footage plus AI enhancement.

Q: Do you still do real ad shoots and video production?
A: Yes — we plan, script and direct real ad shoots and reels productions, and we often blend real footage with AI enhancement for the best of both. The medium follows the story, not the other way around.

Q: What's the difference between SEO, AEO and GEO?
A: SEO gets you ranked in classic search results. AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) gets you chosen as the direct answer — in Google AI Overviews, featured snippets and voice assistants. GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) gets your brand cited and recommended inside AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity.We optimise for all three, because your next customer may never see a classic results page.

Q: How do I get my brand recommended by ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini?
A: AI assistants recommend brands with clear, structured, consistent and widely-corroborated information: schema markup, genuine FAQs, authoritative content, consistent business data across the web, third-party mentions and reviews.That's GEO — and it's a core gaa-tha service. We structure your site and content so generative engines can understand, trust and cite you.

Q: How long does SEO take to show results?
A: Meaningful movement typically shows in 3-6 months, with compounding gains after that. AEO and GEO can move faster — structured answers and schema are often picked up by AI engines within weeks. We pair the slow burn (SEO) with quick wins (AEO/GEO and performance ads) so growth never stalls.

Q: Do you do content marketing and blogging for clients?
